# Filament QR Code

<img src="docs/banner.png" alt="Filament QR &amp; Barcode banner" class="filament-hidden">

[![Latest Version on Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code.svg?style=flat-square)](https://packagist.org/packages/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code)
[![GitHub Tests Action Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code/run-tests.yml?branch=main&label=tests&style=flat-square)](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code/actions?query=workflow%3Arun-tests+branch%3Amain)
[![PHPStan Level 9](https://img.shields.io/badge/PHPStan-level%209-brightgreen.svg?style=flat-square)](https://phpstan.org/)
[![Total Downloads](https://img.shields.io/packagist/dt/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code.svg?style=flat-square)](https://packagist.org/packages/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code)

A powerful, modern QR code package designed exclusively for **Filament v5** and **Laravel 12 / 13**.

Features:

- 📷 **Interactive Camera Scanner**: Real-time camera stream, rear-camera prioritization with remembered choice, responsive decode box synced to the on-screen reticle, and image upload fallback with zero CDN latency.
- 🔗 **Sequential Scanning**: One shared camera feed walks through a multi-field checklist (`QrScanSequence`), with editable or locked steps.
- 🔫 **Hardware Scanner Support**: Native burst keystroke detection (<50ms) that absorbs trailing `Enter` keys to prevent premature form submissions.
- 📦 **Batch Collector (Repeaters & Lists)**: Continuous scanning mode with duplicate protection and sound/haptic confirmation for rapid inventory logging.
- 🎨 **Full QR Generator Suite**: Generate SVG & PNG QR codes with captions/text overlays, logo embedding, and schema components for Forms, Tables, Infolists, and Actions.
- 🔊 **Sensory Confirmation**: Instant zero-latency synthesized Web Audio tone and mobile haptic feedback, pitch and duration tunable per component.

## Try it

The [filament-qr-code-example](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example) app demos every component (scanner showcase, cashier POS, work-order sequence, QR customizer, products resource):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example && cd filament-qr-code-example
composer setup            # composer + npm install, .env, key, SQLite migrations, asset build
php artisan db:seed       # admin@example.com / password
composer dev              # http://localhost:8081/admin
```

## Requirements

- PHP `^8.2`, Laravel 12/13, Filament v5.
- PNG generation needs `gd` or `imagick` plus system fonts (`fonts-dejavu-core` on Debian).
- Camera scanning needs a secure context (`https` or `localhost`).
- The camera bundle (`html5-qrcode`) is compiled into `resources/dist/` — no CDN. After changing anything under `resources/js` or `resources/css`, rebuild with `npm run build` (CI fails when committed `dist/` is stale).

---

## How it works

- **Camera scanning** runs fully in the browser: a modal viewfinder streams the camera through the bundled decoder. The decoder chunk lazy-loads on first camera use; pages that only render QR images never fetch it.
- **Hardware scanners** emulate keyboards: they burst keystrokes in a few dozen milliseconds and end with a terminator key (`Enter`/`Tab`). The interceptor buffers bursts, swallows the terminator so forms don't submit, and routes the value to the active field.
- **Sequences and collectors** write through `$wire.set` into your Livewire form state, so scanned values behave like typed input (validation and reactivity included). Camera DOM lives under `wire:ignore` so Livewire morphs never kill a running feed.
- **Generation** is server-side: renders are cached in-process plus in the Laravel cache, so repeated values encode once. Table modal previews load lazily through a signed image route instead of embedding a data-URI per row.

---

## Getting started in 5 minutes

1. **Install** the package:

   ```bash
   composer require mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code
   ```

2. **Register the plugin** in your panel provider. This step is optional, because the service provider registers the JS and CSS for every panel, but it keeps the setup explicit:

   ```php
   use Filament\Panel;
   use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\FilamentQrCodePlugin;

   public function panel(Panel $panel): Panel
   {
       return $panel
           // ...
           ->plugin(FilamentQrCodePlugin::make());
   }
   ```

3. **Add the package views to your theme.** Buttons, overlays and layout use Tailwind classes in the package views, so your panel theme must scan them. Create a theme if you don't have one (`php artisan make:filament-theme`), add the `@source` line, then run `npm run build`:

   ```css
   /* resources/css/filament/admin/theme.css */
   @source '../../../../vendor/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code/resources/views/**/*';
   ```

4. **Publish the assets** (run it again after every package update):

   ```bash
   php artisan filament:assets
   ```

5. **Add your first field** to a resource form:

   ```php
   use Filament\Schemas\Schema;
   use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\BarcodeFormat;
   use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

   public static function configure(Schema $schema): Schema
   {
       return $schema->components([
           QrScanner::make('sku')
               ->label('SKU')
               ->formats([BarcodeFormat::QrCode, BarcodeFormat::Code128]),
       ]);
   }
   ```

**Expected result:** the form shows a text input with a camera button. The button opens a modal viewfinder. It needs `https` or `localhost` and asks for camera permission. The modal also has an image-upload fallback. A decoded code fills the input and closes the modal. A USB or Bluetooth gun typing into the focused input fills it too, and its `Enter` doesn't submit the form. If the buttons look unstyled, step 3 is missing. Run `php artisan qr-code:doctor` to check your setup.

The full walkthrough, with config publishing, symbologies and a first server check, is in [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md).

---

## Usage

### Which component do I need?

| Job                                                 | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Why not the others                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One input scanned by camera, upload, typing, or gun | [`QrScanner`](docs/scanning.md#qr-scanner-field-qrscanner)                                                                                                                                                            | Sequence/collector add moving parts a single field doesn't need.                   |
| Cashier/POS gun, no camera UI                       | [`QrHardwareScannerListener`](docs/scanning.md#station-listener-qrhardwarescannerlistener) + [one funnel method](docs/scanning.md#step-2--funnel-every-scan-into-one-method)                                    | `QrScanner`'s field listener would double-handle the same burst.                   |
| One camera walking many fields in order             | [`QrScanSequence`](docs/scanning.md#scan-sequence-container-qrscansequence)                                                                                                                                      | Chained `nextField()` hops between separate cameras; the sequence shares one feed. |
| Two fields, hand focus from one to the next         | [`QrScanner::nextField()`](docs/scanning.md#sequential-field-scanning-nextfield)                                                                                                                                              | A sequence is overkill without a shared checklist.                                 |
| Many scans into one list (stocktake, receiving)     | [`QrCollector` / `QrCollectAction`](docs/collecting.md#batch-collector-scanning-qrcollector-qrcollectaction)                                                                                                                     | Sequences map one scan to one field; collectors append.                            |
| Show a QR (form, table, infolist, download)         | [`QrCodeDisplay`](docs/generating.md#in-form-schemas) / [`QrColumn`](docs/generating.md#in-table-columns) / [`QrEntry`](docs/generating.md#in-infolists) / [`DownloadQrAction`](docs/generating.md#as-a-download-action) | Scanner components capture; these only render.                                     |
| Many QRs out at once (labels, handover)             | [`DownloadQrBulkAction`](docs/generating.md#as-a-bulk-zip-export) + print sheet                                                                                                                                          | Single downloads don't scale past a handful of rows.                               |

## Troubleshooting

Run the built-in checks first:

```bash
php artisan qr-code:doctor
```

| Symptom                                      | Likely cause                                                              | Fix                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Camera modal says no devices / access denied | Page served over plain `http` (not `localhost`)                           | Serve via `https` or test on `localhost`; browsers block cameras in insecure contexts.                                                            |
| Camera modal empty on first open             | Permission not granted yet, labels unavailable                            | Grant permission, reopen; the remembered `localStorage` choice wins afterwards.                                                                   |
| Unstyled buttons, layout differs from the panel | Panel theme doesn't `@source` the package views                    | Add `@source '../../../../vendor/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code/resources/views/**/*';` to your theme CSS and rebuild ([Styling](docs/getting-started.md#3-add-the-package-views-to-your-theme)). |
| Stale scanner UI after updating the package  | Committed `dist/` rebuilt but host serving old assets                     | `npm run build` in the package, then `php artisan filament:assets` in the host app.                                                               |
| PNG looks wrong / text overlay is blocky     | Missing GD/Imagick or system fonts                                        | Install `gd` or `imagick` plus `fonts-dejavu-core`; the service falls back to GD bitmap fonts otherwise.                                          |
| Sequence submit misses scanned values        | The form reads the steps from a different place than the sequence writes them | Give the sequence `->statePath()` and read it via `mergeSequenceState()`; the flat `{form}.{step}` paths follow the schema `statePath()`. |
| Same burst handled twice                     | A custom key handler next to the package's wedge router                   | Register the handler with `FilamentQrCode.router.register()` so each burst has one owner ([Extension points](docs/extending.md#browser)).         |
| Typed text becomes a "scan"                  | `minBarcodeLength` too low for a keyboard-heavy form                      | Raise `minBarcodeLength` to 4–6 on that component.                                                                                                |
| Scan lands in the wrong input (e.g. search)  | Station Listener fell back to the first empty form input                  | `QrHardwareScannerListener::make([...])->fallbackToAnyInput(false)` (or `hardware_scanner.fallback_to_any_input => false`); listen for `qr-scan-unrouted`. |
| A slow or Bluetooth gun's short codes are missed | `min_fast_keys` (default 3) needs three fast gaps in a row               | Lower it on that component with `->minFastKeys(1)` (or `hardware_scanner.min_fast_keys`).                                                         |
| `nextField()` / listener misses a field      | Name does not match exactly                                               | Use the exact field name; nested paths like `items.0.sku` are supported, and `sku` never matches `parent_sku`.                                   |
| Table page is slow with many QRs             | Eager modal data-URIs per row                                             | Keep `->lazyModal()` (default) and the persistent cache enabled; tune `generator.cache_ttl`.                                                      |

## Security notes

Lazy modal previews are served by the signed `filamentQrCode.image` route. Signatures already stop tampering; if QR data or logo paths can come from users, turn on the opt-in hardening (all off by default): `generator.logo_base_paths` limits logos to listed directories, and `image_route.ttl` / `throttle` / `strict_colors` add expiring URLs, a rate limit and `#rrggbb`-only colours. See [Image route security](docs/generating.md#image-route-security).

## Reporting issues

1. Run `php artisan qr-code:doctor` and include its output.
2. Include your PHP / Laravel / Filament versions (`php -v`, `composer show laravel/framework filament/filament`), plus for camera issues the browser and whether the page is served over `https`/`localhost`, and for gun issues the scanner model and its suffix keys.
3. Describe expected vs actual, with a minimal schema snippet that reproduces it.

Security vulnerabilities are handled privately — see [Security Vulnerabilities](#security-vulnerabilities), not public issues.

# Getting started

> Back to [README](../README.md) · [Scanning](scanning.md) · [Generating](generating.md) · [Reference](reference.md) · [FAQ](faq.md)

This page takes you from `composer require` to a field that checks scans on the server. Each step lists what you should see before you move on.

Requirements: PHP `^8.2`, Laravel 12 or 13, and Filament v5. Camera scanning needs a secure context (`https` or `localhost`). PNG output needs `gd` or `imagick`.

## 1. Install the package

```bash
composer require mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code
```

The service provider is auto-discovered. It registers the JS and CSS with Filament for every panel.

## 2. Register the plugin

Registering the plugin is optional, because the assets load without it. It keeps the setup explicit, and `FilamentQrCodePlugin::get()` needs it.

```php
use Filament\Panel;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\FilamentQrCodePlugin;

public function panel(Panel $panel): Panel
{
    return $panel
        // ...
        ->plugin(FilamentQrCodePlugin::make());
}
```

## 3. Add the package views to your theme

The package CSS only styles the scanner chrome (viewfinder, reticle, flash states). Buttons, overlays and layout use Tailwind utility classes in the package views, and Tailwind only generates classes found in the files it scans. Create a theme if the panel has none (`php artisan make:filament-theme`), then add the package views to its `@source` list:

```css
/* resources/css/filament/admin/theme.css */
@import '../../../../vendor/filament/filament/resources/css/theme.css';

@source '../../../../app/Filament';
@source '../../../../resources/views/filament';
@source '../../../../vendor/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code/resources/views/**/*';
```

Run `npm run build` afterwards. If you skip this step, the Start/Stop buttons are unstyled, overlays collapse, and the modal looks different from the rest of the panel.

## 4. Publish the assets

```bash
php artisan filament:assets
```

This copies the scanner bundle and the camera decoder into `public/`. The decoder is a separate module, about 120 KB gzipped. It loads on first camera use, so pages that only render QR images never fetch it. Run the command again after every package update.

## 5. Add your first field

```php
use Filament\Schemas\Schema;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\BarcodeFormat;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

public static function configure(Schema $schema): Schema
{
    return $schema->components([
        QrScanner::make('sku')
            ->label('SKU')
            ->formats([BarcodeFormat::QrCode, BarcodeFormat::Code128]),
    ]);
}
```

`formats()` limits the camera to the symbologies you actually scan. That speeds up decoding and cuts false positives. The cases are `QrCode`, `Aztec`, `DataMatrix`, `Maxicode`, `Codabar`, `Code39`, `Code93`, `Code128`, `Itf`, `Ean13`, `Ean8`, `UpcA` and `UpcE`.

**What you should see:**

- A text input with a camera button.
- The button opens a modal viewfinder after the browser asks for camera permission. Over plain `http`, the modal explains that it needs a secure context.
- The modal has an image-upload fallback.
- A decoded code fills the input and closes the modal.
- A USB or Bluetooth gun (a keyboard-wedge Hardware Scanner) typing into the focused input fills it too. The gun's `Enter` is swallowed, so the form doesn't submit.

## 6. Check the scan on the server

Live scans write straight into the Livewire state. To accept only codes that match a record, add a lookup. A scan that matches nothing is rejected before it is kept:

```php
use App\Models\Product;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('sku')
    ->lookup(Product::class, 'sku')
    ->onScanned(fn (string $code, $record) => logger()->info("Scanned {$record?->name}"));
```

Accepted scans flash green and rejected ones flash red with a beep and vibration. More checks (`validateUsing()`, `rejectWhen()`, `pipe()`) are in [Server-side checks](scanning.md#server-side-checks).

## 7. Tune the defaults (optional)

```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag="filament-qr-code-config"
```

`config/qr-code.php` holds the defaults for the camera, the Hardware Scanner Interceptor, feedback, sequences, the generator and auditing. Every key is in [Reference](reference.md#configuration). A setter on a component always wins over config.

## When something is off

```bash
php artisan qr-code:doctor
```

The doctor checks the image backends, fonts, published assets, config and routes. The [Troubleshooting table](../README.md#troubleshooting) and the [FAQ](faq.md) cover the usual symptoms.

## Where next

- Pick a component: [Which component do I need?](../README.md#which-component-do-i-need)
- Guns without a camera UI: [Station Listener](scanning.md#station-listener-qrhardwarescannerlistener)
- One camera filling many fields: [Scan Sequence Container](scanning.md#scan-sequence-container-qrscansequence)
- Many scans into one list: [Batch Collector Scanning](collecting.md)
- Showing QR codes: [Generating](generating.md)

<!-- file: docs/scanning.md -->

# Scanning

> Back to [README](../README.md) · [Batch collecting](collecting.md) · [Generating](generating.md) · [Reference](reference.md)

QR Scanner Fields, the Station Listener, the Scan Sequence Container, Sequential Field Scanning with `nextField()`, and the cashier POS tutorial. Vocabulary follows [CONTEXT.md](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code/blob/main/CONTEXT.md).

## QR Scanner Field (`QrScanner`)

![Scanner modal with the camera open](images/scanner-modal-camera.png)

*The scanner modal with a live camera feed (Chromium fake camera shown).* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Pages/ScannerShowcase.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Pages/ScannerShowcase.php).

Add a QR scanner field to your form schema with camera modal and hardware scanner integration:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\BarcodeFormat;

QrScanner::make('sku')
    ->label('Product SKU / Barcode')
    ->formats([
        BarcodeFormat::QrCode,
        BarcodeFormat::Code128,
        BarcodeFormat::Code39,
        BarcodeFormat::Ean13,
    ])
    ->sound(true)
    ->vibrate(true)
    ->hardwareScanner(enabled: true, burstThresholdMs: 50)
    ->afterStateUpdated(function ($component, ?string $state): void {
        // Live-scan normalization belongs here: scanFormat() below never
        // runs on live camera/hardware scans (server-side hook only).
        $normalized = filled($state) ? strtoupper(trim($state)) : $state;

        if ($normalized !== $state) {
            $component->state($normalized);
        }
    });
```

Option reference:

- `formats()` — symbologies the decoder attempts. Omit only when truly unknown. With no filter the effective `fps` auto-degrades 25 → 12 against main-thread lag (explicit `fps()` always wins).
- `scanFormat()` / `onScan()` — programmatic-only hooks; they do **not** run on live camera or hardware scans. Normalize live values with `normalizeUsing()` — see [Normalize live scans](customizing.md#normalize-live-scans).
- `hardwareScanner(terminators: [...], minBarcodeLength: 2)` — burst tuning. Buffers are sanitized (STX/ETX/CR/LF stripped, mirroring `HasHardwareScanner::sanitizeScannedValue()`), IME compositions never count, and terminator-less guns flush after `scanTimeoutMs` (default 150).
- `scanRules(['min:3'])` — submit-time validation for scanned values. `rejectWhen(fn ($state) => ..., 'message')` clears bad live scans immediately and dispatches a `qr-scan-rejected` window event (with `{ message }`) so the app can notify.
- `hardwareInput(scope: HardwareInputScope::Page)` — also catch wedge scans when no scan field has focus (default `Focus`: only while focused; config `hardware_scanner.default_scope`). A focused scan field always wins.
- `nextField('other')` — focuses that field after a scan (field handoff, see §4).
- `fps()` / `qrbox()` — defaults 25 / 250. `qrbox` is a _maximum_: the actual decode box scales to the viewfinder and the green reticle follows it.
- `preferRearCamera()` — rear heuristic, but the operator's last camera choice (stored in `localStorage`) always wins.
- `allowUpload(false)` — hides the image-file fallback.
- `beepFrequency()` / `beepDuration()` / `vibrateDuration()` — feedback tuning.

The modal lists every detected camera (switching restarts the feed and is remembered) and closes automatically after a successful camera scan. Upload scans reuse the same decoder instance.

> Hardware scanner note: all hardware consumers share one page-wide input router, so a burst is never handled twice, even with a `QrScanner`, a `QrHardwareScannerListener` and a `QrCollector` on the same page. See [Hardware routing](reference.md#hardware-routing).

## Station Listener (`QrHardwareScannerListener`)

![Cashier page driven by the station listener](images/cashier-station-listener.png)

*A hardware scanner feeds the cart through the station listener.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Pages/CashierCheckout.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Pages/CashierCheckout.php).

For manufacturing stations and warehouse counters where operators shoot barcodes without touching the mouse:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrHardwareScannerListener;

QrHardwareScannerListener::make([
    'step',
    'employee',
    'document',
    'equipment',
])
    ->autoFocusNext(true)
    ->sound(true);
```

Add `QrHardwareScannerListener` anywhere in your schema. It intercepts hardware scanner bursts across the entire page, syncs Livewire state, and auto-advances focus. Each burst is routed to:

1. the focused input or textarea, otherwise
2. the first empty registered field (in the order passed to `make([...])`), otherwise
3. the first empty `text`, `search`, `number` input or textarea in any form on the page — only while `fallbackToAnyInput()` is enabled (default `true`, config `hardware_scanner.fallback_to_any_input`).

Step 3 can catch a search or filter box. Turn it off so scans only land in the focused or registered fields:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrHardwareScannerListener;

QrHardwareScannerListener::make(['sku', 'quantity'])
    ->fallbackToAnyInput(false);
```

When no target is found, nothing is written and the listener dispatches a `qr-scan-unrouted` window event with `{ value }`, so the app can warn the operator:

```blade
<div x-on:qr-scan-unrouted.window="alert(`No field for ${$event.detail.value}`)"></div>
```

Fields are matched by their exact name — `data-field-name`, `name`, `id`, or a `wire:model` path equal to the name or ending in `.<name>` — so `sku` never matches `parent_sku`, and nested names such as `items.0.sku` work in `make([...])` and `nextField()`.

The interceptor buffers keystrokes and treats gaps under `burstThresholdMs` (default 50) as a scanner burst. On a terminator key with a long-enough buffer, it `preventDefault()`s (no accidental submit), sanitizes, and routes the value — the delivery point (field, sequence, collector, or this listener) then plays the single confirmation beep, so one burst always yields one beep. Tune `terminators` and `minBarcodeLength` to your gun's suffix.

Held-down keys (keyboard auto-repeat) never count toward a burst, so holding a key and pressing Enter is not a scan. For keyboard-heavy forms, require more consecutive fast keystrokes before a terminator counts with `minFastKeys()` (default `3`, config `hardware_scanner.min_fast_keys`; `1` accepts a single fast gap like 0.x did):

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('sku')
    ->minFastKeys(3);

// or together with the other interceptor options
QrScanner::make('sku')
    ->hardwareScanner(terminators: ['Enter'], minBarcodeLength: 4, minFastKeys: 3);
```

`hardwareScanner(...)` resets every interceptor option to its signature default, so pass all the options you care about in one call (or use the dedicated setters such as `minFastKeys()` and `scanTimeout()`).

## Scan Sequence Container (`QrScanSequence`)

Sequential scanning means **one scanner driving multiple fields**: a single shared camera feed (or one handheld gun) walks through a checklist. That is `QrScanSequence`:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\BarcodeFormat;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;

QrScanSequence::make([
    'step' => 'Operation Step',
    'employee' => 'Employee ID',
    'document' => 'Document Number',
    'equipment' => 'Equipment Code',
])
    ->fps(25)
    ->qrbox(250)
    ->formats([BarcodeFormat::QrCode, BarcodeFormat::Code128])
    ->preferRearCamera()
    ->sound(true)
    ->vibrate(true);
```

One feed, one checklist: steps auto-advance, clicking a step re-targets it, and the camera dropdown matches the single-field scanner. It renders stacked on mobile and split-screen on desktop. When the last step lands, the feed stops by itself so the button never gets stuck on "Stop".

Each step value is also written to `{schema state path}.{step}` (for example `data.step`), so a form that reads the steps as separate fields keeps working; the prefix always follows your schema's `statePath()`. Live values are normalized with `normalizeStepUsing()` (applied on read/merge; a sequence with a step normalizer checks each scan on the server, so the step list shows the normalized code) — see [Normalize live scans](customizing.md#normalize-live-scans); `scanFormat()` / `onStepScanned()` are programmatic-only — see [Drive scans programmatically](customizing.md#drive-scans-programmatically).

### Reading sequence state

Give the container its own state and read it back through helpers:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;

QrScanSequence::make(['batch_number', 'serial_number'])
    ->statePath('sequence')
    ->normalizeStepUsing(fn ($rawValue) => strtoupper(trim((string) $rawValue)));

// In your submit handler:
$sequence = /* resolve the QrScanSequence component */;
$state = $sequence->mergeSequenceState($this->form->getState());

if (! $sequence->isSequenceComplete($state)) {
    Notification::make()->title('Incomplete sequence')->warning()->send();
    return;
}
```

The container writes via `$wire.set`, syncing both the component state and the legacy prefix paths — so read with `mergeSequenceState()` and validate with `isSequenceComplete()`, never a hand-rolled `array_merge` over `$this->data`. Without `->statePath()`, `getSequenceState()` falls back to the legacy paths. `getMissingSequenceKeys()` lists what's still empty.

### Correcting a scan (unedited vs edited values)

Every step is a plain input: scans fill it, and operators can type or fix any value by hand — handy for unreadable labels. Every change syncs to the bound Livewire state and dispatches `qr-sequence-edited`. Pass `->editable(false)` to render locked read-only values instead. To flip modes live without a re-render wiping the running feed, dispatch `qr-sequence-editable` with `{ enabled }` on `window`; the component listens for it (its DOM is `wire:ignore`d so scans survive Livewire morphs).

### Checked steps and auto-submit

Describe each step with `ScanStep` to check scans on the server and submit the form once the whole set is in:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\InvalidSequenceBehavior;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanStep;

QrScanSequence::make()
    ->statePath('receipt') // recommended: the key server checks use (or ->key('receipt'))
    ->steps([
        ScanStep::make('po')->label('Purchase order')->validateUsing(['regex:/^PO-\d+$/']),
        ScanStep::make('sku')->lookup(Product::class, 'sku'),
        ScanStep::make('lot')->validateUsing(['regex:/^L\d{3}$/'])->optional(),
        ScanStep::make('serial')->validateUsing(fn (string $code): ?string => str_starts_with($code, 'SN') ? null : 'Not a serial.'),
    ])
    ->validateAllUsing(fn (array $values): array => $values['po'] === $values['serial'] ? ['serial' => 'Serial repeats the PO.'] : [])
    ->onInvalidSequence(InvalidSequenceBehavior::JumpToStep) // or Restart
    ->onCompleted(fn (array $values) => /* ... */)
    ->autoSubmit()          // calls the Livewire submit() method
    ->resetAfterSubmit();   // or ->continuous() to start over after every set
```

- **One request per scan.** Each scan calls `handleStepScan` once. The server checks the step (rules, then lookup, then closures, the same pipeline as `QrScanner`), writes the value, and answers with the step to show next. A rejected scan keeps the operator on that step and shows the message.
- **Optional steps.** An optional step whose check fails gives way when the code fits the next step: the next step takes the code and the optional one stays empty. An optional step without checks accepts everything, so it never gives way.
- **Whole-set checks.** `validateAllUsing()` runs once every required step has a value. Rules are keyed by step (`['po' => 'different:serial']`); unkeyed rules apply to the last step. A closure returns `null` or `[]` to pass, a message (last step) or `[step => message]`. On failure the default (`jump_to_step`) keeps every value and asks for the failing step again (when the failing step is a repeat step and the last scan filled it, that code is dropped so the operator can scan the right one); `Restart` clears the steps.
- **Completion.** `onCompleted($values)` runs and `ScanSequenceCompleted` fires, then `autoSubmit()` calls your submit method (`autoSubmit(method: 'save')` for another name). A `ValidationException` from it lands in the error bag and the values stay.
- **Defaults** live in config `sequence`: `on_invalid` `'jump_to_step'`, `auto_submit` `false`, `submit_method` `'submit'`, `reset_after_submit` `false`, `continuous` `false`.
- **Plain sequences don't change.** Without checks, `validateAllUsing()`, `onCompleted()`, `autoSubmit()` or `continuous()`, the browser writes state itself as before and makes no request. `fields([...])` is shorthand for steps without checks.
- **Browser events.** `qr-sequence-step` (now with `skipped` and `source`), `qr-sequence-completed` (now with `submitted`), plus `qr-sequence-rejected` `{ field, value, message, source }` and `qr-sequence-invalid` `{ field, message, values }`.

- **Normal submits check too.** `$this->form->getState()` re-runs every step check (on the step's state path) and `validateAllUsing()` (reported on the last step once every required step has a value). Empty steps pass; add `required` yourself if you need it.
- **Typed corrections.** In an editable sequence with server work, an edited step is checked like a scan with source `ScanInput::Manual` (`'manual'`). It never skips an optional step or moves the current step, and a rejected edit stays visible with its message.
- **Keys.** Server checks reach the component by its key. Give the sequence `statePath()` or `key()`; if it has neither, it gets an automatic key from its step keys (`qr-scan-sequence-po-sku`) and logs a warning in the local environment, so two identical sequences on one page need explicit keys.

### Handheld scanners, sticky and repeat steps

A keyboard-wedge scanner fills the sequence without any focus: every burst goes to the current step, then the sequence moves on. If an operator focuses a step's input, the next burst goes to that step instead. While a server check is running, one burst waits and replays; any more are dropped (`qr-scan-dropped`).

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\RepeatComplete;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanStep;

QrScanSequence::make()
    ->statePath('picking')
    ->steps([
        ScanStep::make('po')->sticky(),                      // kept for every item
        ScanStep::make('sku')->lookup(Product::class, 'sku'),
        ScanStep::make('serials')
            ->repeat(fn (array $values): int => Product::firstWhere('sku', $values['sku'] ?? null)?->serial_count ?? 1),
        ScanStep::make('extras')->repeat()->finishWith('DONE')->optional(), // open-ended
    ])
    ->continuous();
```

- **`sticky()`** keeps the step's value when the sequence resets (`resetAfterSubmit()`, `continuous()`, `onInvalidSequence(Restart)`). After a reset the sequence starts at the first empty step. To change a sticky value, press its **Clear** button (or select the step and scan again).
- **`repeat(n)`** collects `n` codes into a list (`['P1', 'P2', 'P3']`). Every code runs the step's checks, and a code already in the list is rejected unless the step has `allowDuplicates()`. The step shows `k / n`. Each code has a small remove button for mis-scans. `n` can be a closure that receives `$values`; if it throws (say, it reads a step that has no value yet), the step acts as open-ended until it can be counted, and a warning is logged in the local environment.
- **When a repeat step is full**, config `sequence.repeat_complete` decides what happens: `'advance'` (default) moves to the next step; `'wait'` stays on the step and rejects further codes until the operator finishes it. Override it per step with `onRepeatComplete(RepeatComplete::Wait)`.
- **`repeat()` without a count** is open-ended: it keeps collecting until the operator finishes it.
- **Finishing a step**: scan the finish code (config `sequence.finish_code` for every step, default `null` = none; `finishWith('DONE')` overrides it per step) or press the step's **Done** button. A step needs at least one code (or all `n` in `wait` mode) before it can finish. The finish code is never stored.
- Sticky and repeat steps go through the server like checked steps (one `handleStepScan` request per scan). Sequences without them are unchanged.

### Step order: optional skips and `when()`

- **An optional step gives way.** When a live scan (camera or hardware) fails an optional step's checks but passes the next active step, the optional step is skipped (reported in `skipped`) and the code lands there. The next step can be a repeat step, so `po, sku, lot (optional), serials (repeat)` works: a serial scanned at the lot step goes straight into serials.
- **`when()` makes a step conditional.** The closure receives `$values` (the sequence so far) and `$step`, and returns a bool:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanStep;

ScanStep::make('batch')
    ->when(fn (array $values): bool => str_starts_with($values['sku'] ?? '', 'BATCH-'))
    ->validateUsing(['regex:/^B-\d+$/']),
```

  While it returns `false`, the step is skipped and isn't required. Its value is dropped, and it's greyed out in the browser. A scan aimed straight at it is rejected (`step_inactive`) and the sequence moves to the next empty active step. Conditions run in step order, so a step's closure sees the values of the active steps before it. A closure that throws counts as active, and a warning is logged in the local environment.

### Driving a sequence from page code

Call these on the component from your page. Each one updates the browser on the next response.

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;

$sequence = $this->form->getComponent(fn ($component) => $component instanceof QrScanSequence);

$sequence->goToStep('lot');                      // move the cursor
$sequence->resetSequence();                      // start over, keeping sticky steps
$sequence->resetSequence(keepSticky: false, values: ['po' => 'PO-7001']); // seed values
$sequence->setRepeatCount('serials', 5);         // override repeat() for this page; null clears it
```

`setRepeatCount()` is stored in the session, keyed by the Livewire component, so later server checks agree with the counter. Most pages don't need it: a `repeat()` closure that reads page state already updates the `k / n` counter on every re-render (see [Runtime control](#runtime-control)).

## Sequential Field Scanning (`nextField()`)

Move focus to the next field after each scan (a two-field handoff — distinct from sequential scanning above):

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('batch_number')
    ->nextField('serial_number'),

QrScanner::make('serial_number')
    ->nextField('location_code'),

QrScanner::make('location_code'),
```

---

## Tutorial: Cashier POS with a Handheld Scanner

Cashiers scan with a physical gun, so there is **no camera UI** — just an input box and the invisible hardware scanner interceptor catching bursts anywhere on the page.

### Step 1 — mount the hardware scanner listener

A Filament page needs a schema to host the component:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrHardwareScannerListener;

public ?array $data = [];

public function form(Schema $schema): Schema
{
    return $schema->statePath('data')->components([
        QrHardwareScannerListener::make(['scanInput'])
            ->autoFocusNext(false) // stay on the SKU box for rapid scans
            ->sound(true)
            ->fallbackToAnyInput(false) // never drop scans into search or filter boxes
            ->hardwareScanner(terminators: ['Enter', 'Tab'], minBarcodeLength: 2, minFastKeys: 3),
    ]);
}
```

Render `{{ $this->form }}` — it outputs nothing visible.

`fallbackToAnyInput(false)` is recommended for a till: a scan goes to the focused input or `scanInput`, and anything else raises `qr-scan-unrouted` instead of landing in an unrelated box. `minFastKeys: 3` keeps a cashier's fast typing from being taken for a scan.

### Step 2 — funnel every scan into one method

Gun bursts and typed input must converge, or quantities double-count:

```blade
<div x-on:qr-hardware-scanned.window="$wire.scanProduct($event.detail.value)">
```

```php
public function scanProduct(string $code): void
{
    $product = Product::where('sku', trim($code))
        ->orWhere('barcode', trim($code))->first();

    if (! $product) {
        Notification::make()->title('Product Not Found')->danger()->send();
        return;
    }

    // bump quantity if already in cart, else push a new line
}
```

Keep the manual input's Enter handler: scanner bursts swallow their terminator (`preventFormSubmit`), so Enter only fires for typed input — no double-adds.

## Server-side checks

![Server-side check accepting a scan](images/server-checks-accepted.png)

*A scan accepted by the server-side rules.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Pages/ServerSideChecks.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Pages/ServerSideChecks.php).

![Server-side check rejecting an out-of-stock scan](images/server-checks-rejected.png)

*An out-of-stock scan rejected with an inline error.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Pages/ServerSideChecks.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Pages/ServerSideChecks.php).

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('sku')
    ->validateUsing(['required', 'string', 'max:32'])
    ->lookup(Product::class, 'sku', modifyQueryUsing: fn (Builder $query) => $query->where('active', true))
    ->validateUsing(fn (string $code, ?Product $record): ?string => $record?->stock > 0 ? null : __('Out of stock'))
    ->cooldown(1500);
```

- Checks run on every live scan and again when the form is submitted, always in this order: rules, lookup, closures. The first failure stops the scan.
- A closure returns `null` or `true` to pass, a message to fail, or `false` to fail with the generic message.
- Name the closure parameter `$record` to receive the lookup result. A `Model`-typed parameter with another name receives the form's record instead.
- `cooldown()` sets how long the browser ignores a repeated code. Fields with checks default to `qr-code.scan.cooldown_ms` (1500 ms); fields without checks default to 0. Use `cooldown(0)` to turn it off. The browser enforces it: a repeat within the window fires `qr-scan-duplicate` and is not sent to the server.

### Reacting to scans

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanResult;

QrScanner::make('sku')
    ->lookup(Product::class, 'sku')
    ->onScanned(function (ScanResult $result, Set $set): void {
        $set('price', $result->record->price);
    })
    ->onRejected(fn (ScanResult $result) => Notification::make()->danger()->title($result->message)->send())
    ->clearOnReject(); // default from qr-code.scan.clear_on_reject
```

- `onScanned` and `onRejected` run for live scans only, never when the form is submitted.
- Callbacks can ask for `ScanResult $result`, `Get $get`, `Set $set`, `string $code`, `$record` (named), `?ScanInput $source`, `$component` and `$livewire`.
- Accepted live scans fire `ScanAccepted` and `QrCodeScanned` (with `source` `camera`, `hardware` or `upload`); rejected ones fire `ScanRejected`. With `qr-code.audit.enabled`, accepted live scans are logged.
- If `onScanned` throws, the field keeps its previous value, the error is reported, and the scan is rejected with the generic message.
- Configuring `onScanned` or `onRejected` alone makes the field call the server on every scan and enables the default cooldown.

### In the browser

- A field with server checks sends each scan to the server once and waits for the answer. While it waits, the camera pauses and further scans are ignored.
- Accepted: the value stays, the success beep plays, and `qr-scan-accepted` and `qr-scanned` fire. Camera scans close the scanner.
- Rejected: the field clears (unless `clearOnReject(false)`), `qr-scan-rejected` fires once with the message, and the camera resumes so you can scan again.
- If the request fails, the scan is rejected with "The scan could not be checked. Please try again."
- The same code scanned again within the cooldown is ignored and fires `qr-scan-duplicate`.
- A page-level `QrHardwareScannerListener` hands bursts to a server-checked field, so wedge scans are checked too.

### Continuous mode

For POS line entry (scan, scan, scan) put the field in continuous mode. Every accepted code runs `onScanned()` once, and the field is ready for the next code straight away.

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\ContinuousDisplay;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\HardwareInputScope;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\ScanMode;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('scan')
    ->mode(ScanMode::Continuous)
    ->hardwareInput(scope: HardwareInputScope::Page) // catch wedge scans anywhere on the page
    ->lookup(Product::class, 'sku')
    ->onScanned(fn (Product $record, Get $get, Set $set) => $set('lines', addLine($get('lines'), $record)))
    ->continuousDisplay(ContinuousDisplay::Empty) // default; LastCode keeps the code in the field
    ->pauseOnReject(false)                         // default: show the error and keep scanning
    ->keepCameraOpen(false)                        // default: close the camera after each scan
    ->dehydrated(false);
```

- Each code is one server call (`handleScan`), even without rules or a lookup, because that is where `onScanned()` runs. Merging lines (same SKU twice = quantity 2) is your job in `onScanned()`.
- After an accepted scan the server clears the field (`continuousDisplay(ContinuousDisplay::Empty)`, the default) or keeps the code (`LastCode`). A `$set()` on the field's own path inside `onScanned()` is overwritten by the clear.
- A rejected scan shows its message under the field. By default scanning carries on. With `pauseOnReject()` the field stops taking scans until the operator presses **Resume scanning** (or Escape); `qr-scan-paused` and `qr-scan-resumed` fire.
- The camera closes after each accepted scan by default; `keepCameraOpen()` keeps it running for the next code.
- A repeat of the same code within 300 ms is ignored (`qr-code.scan.continuous.cooldown_ms`; `cooldown()` overrides). Raise it if a camera re-reads codes; lower it if cashiers scan the same item twice very quickly.
- A wedge scan that arrives while the field is still checking the previous one is queued (one slot) and checked next. Any further scan in that window is dropped and fires `qr-scan-dropped`.
- A continuous field is usually empty at submit, so don't make it `required()`. If you do, a warning is logged once in the local environment.

See the [POS recipe](recipes/pos.md) for a full page.

### Feedback

Fields with server checks give a different cue for each outcome:

| Outcome | Sound | Vibration | Flash |
|---|---|---|---|
| Accepted | one tone (`beepFrequency`, `beepDuration`) | `[100]` | green |
| Rejected or check failed | two low tones | `[80, 60, 80]` | red |
| Duplicate (within cooldown) | none | none | none |

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('sku')
    ->lookup(Product::class, 'sku')
    ->beep(success: true, error: true)
    ->vibrate(success: [50], error: [200, 100, 200])
    ->flash(); // or flash(false)
```

Defaults live in `qr-code.feedback.success` and `qr-code.feedback.error`. `sound(false)` and `vibrate(false)` still turn everything off. Fields without checks keep the single success beep. The ring lasts about 0.9 s on the field; while the scanner modal is open it flashes the modal panel instead, and the field ring plays once the modal closes.

## Camera decoder, torch and zoom

The camera picks its decoder on first use: the browser's native `BarcodeDetector` when it supports every format the field asks for, otherwise the bundled html5-qrcode. Swap it from page JavaScript before any camera starts:

```js
window.FilamentQrCode.qrCameraCore.setDecoder(({ formats }) => myDecoderModule);
```

The loader returns an html5-qrcode-shaped module; see the [ZXing recipe](recipes/zxing-decoder.md) for a complete adapter. `setDecoder(null)` restores the default.

Torch and zoom controls appear in the viewfinder when the running camera reports `torch` or `zoom` (typically Chrome on Android). Hide them with `->cameraControls(false)` or `qr-code.camera.controls`. iOS Safari reports neither, so the controls stay hidden there.

## Runtime control

Scanners and sequences follow the server after they're mounted. You can also drive them from page JavaScript.

### Options follow the server

When a re-render changes a field's options (say a `pauseOnReject(fn () => $this->pauseOnReject)` closure flips), the browser applies them **without re-creating the component**. The camera, the queued scan and the field state all survive. The options travel on a `data-qr-options` attribute that Livewire morphs. For a sequence, it sits on a wrapper outside the `wire:ignore`d UI, so repeat counts, labels, active steps and values follow the server too.

The current scan always finishes first:

- New options wait for a server check that's running.
- Camera options (`fps`, `qrbox`, `formats`, `preferRearCamera`) apply on the next camera start.
- A sequence keeps its list of steps until the round completes or resets. Everything else (repeat counts, labels, active steps) applies right away.

To apply changes only when you ask, set config `scan.sync_options` to `'refresh'` or use a per-field override, then send a refresh event:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\OptionsSync;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('sku')->syncOptions(OptionsSync::Refresh);
// later, from PHP or JS:
$this->dispatch('qr-scanner-refresh', field: 'data.sku');
```

### Per-element API

```js
const scanner = document.querySelector('[data-field-name="sku"]').qrScanner; // root has data-qr-scanner
await scanner.feed('PRD-1001');            // runs the same path as a scan (source defaults to 'hardware')
scanner.pause(); scanner.resume();
scanner.reset();                           // clear value, error, queued scan and the duplicate cooldown
scanner.setOptions({ mode: 'continuous', pauseOnReject: true });
scanner.refresh();                         // re-read the rendered options now
scanner.getOptions(); scanner.getState();  // { value, isPaused, isChecking, isScanning }

const sequence = document.querySelector('[data-qr-sequence]').qrScanSequence;
await sequence.feed('PO-7001');            // into the current step
sequence.goToStep('lot');
sequence.reset({ values: { po: 'PO-7001' } }); // also writes the values to Livewire state
sequence.pause(); sequence.resume();
sequence.setOptions({ ... }); sequence.refresh();
sequence.getOptions(); sequence.getState();    // { currentStep, values, isPaused, isChecking, isScanning }
```

`feed()` accepts `camera`, `hardware`, `upload` or `manual` as its second argument. Typed (`manual`) codes never skip an optional step.

### Window events

Send these on `window` (or with `$this->dispatch(...)` from PHP). `field` picks the target. A scanner matches on its state path (`data.sku`), its field name (`sku`) or its component key (`form.sku`); a sequence matches on its key or its state path. Leave `field` out to reach every component of that kind.

| Event | `detail` |
| --- | --- |
| `qr-scanner-feed` | `{ field, code, source? }` |
| `qr-scanner-pause` / `-resume` / `-reset` / `-refresh` | `{ field }` |
| `qr-scanner-set-options` | `{ field, options }` |
| `qr-sequence-feed` | `{ field, code, source? }` |
| `qr-sequence-go-to` | `{ field, step }` |
| `qr-sequence-reset` | `{ field, values? }` |
| `qr-sequence-pause` / `-resume` / `-refresh` | `{ field }` (a paused sequence shows a "Scanning paused." banner with a Resume button) |
| `qr-sequence-set-options` | `{ field, options }` |
| `qr-sequence-set-repeat` | `{ field, step, count }` (display only; use `setRepeatCount()` in PHP to change the server check too) |

```blade
<x-filament::button x-on:click="$dispatch('qr-scanner-pause', { field: 'data.sku' })">Pause</x-filament::button>
```

### Your own inputs in the hardware router

Every keyboard-wedge burst on the page has exactly one owner. To let a custom input (a keypad, an RFID box, a third-party widget) take part, register it with the shared router:

```js
const unregister = window.FilamentQrCode.router.register({
    id: 'rfid-keypad',                      // unique
    element: document.querySelector('#rfid'), // focus inside this element makes it the owner
    kind: 'custom',
    scope: 'focus',                         // 'focus': only while focused; 'page': also when nothing else has focus
    detection: { minBarcodeLength: 4 },     // optional; burstThresholdMs, minFastKeys, terminators, scanTimeoutMs, preventSubmit
    accept: (code) => true,                 // optional; return false to pass the burst on
    deliver: (code) => console.log('scanned', code),
});
// later
unregister();
```

Optional hooks: `hold(code)` (return `true` to keep a burst while you're busy), `ownsFocus(element)` (claim focus outside `element`), and `candidates()`. The router emits `qr-scan-routed` for every delivery.

<!-- file: docs/collecting.md -->

# Batch Collecting

> Back to [README](../README.md) · [Scanning](scanning.md) · [Generating](generating.md) · [Reference](reference.md)

Continuous camera multi-scan for inventory and repeater flows. For cashier/POS gun flows, see the [POS tutorial](scanning.md#tutorial-cashier-pos-with-a-handheld-scanner).

## Batch Collector Scanning (`QrCollector`, `QrCollectAction`)

![Shelf audit page with three product labels collected and an unknown code flagged by the server-side lookup](images/shelf-audit-collector.png)

*A warehouse shelf audit: each wedge or camera scan is looked up against seeded products, repeats are ignored, and unknown codes are flagged so they can be removed (×) before submitting.*

![Shelf audit after recording a count, with the list cleared and the count listed under Recent counts](images/shelf-audit-recorded.png)

*After "Record count" the collector clears and the count shows which products were not seen.*

See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Pages/ShelfAudit.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Pages/ShelfAudit.php).

### In Form Repeaters

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\BarcodeFormat;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrCollector;

QrCollector::make('scanned_items')
    ->allowDuplicates(false)
    ->delayBetweenScans(1200)
    ->formats([BarcodeFormat::QrCode, BarcodeFormat::Code128])
    ->preferRearCamera();
```

### As a Table / Repeater Action

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\BarcodeFormat;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Tables\Actions\QrCollectAction;

$table->headerActions([
    QrCollectAction::make()
        ->allowDuplicates(false)
        ->formats([BarcodeFormat::QrCode, BarcodeFormat::Code128])
        ->onScan(fn ($code) => logger()->info("Collected {$code}")),
]);
```

Each scan notifies the server through exactly one channel: `$wire.handleCollectorScan($code)` when the host Livewire component defines it, otherwise a `qr-collector-item-added` window event (with `{ code }`) that the host forwards — e.g. `x-on:qr-collector-item-added.window` calling your Livewire method, which can then invoke `$action->handleScan($code)` to run the `onScan` callback. The component picks deterministically, so a scan is never handled twice.

Every `handleScan()` call also fires a `QrCodeScanned` event — see [Audit scans](customizing.md#audit-scans).

Custom terminators and minimum lengths are configurable via `->hardwareScanner(terminators: [...], minBarcodeLength: 3)` and feedback pitch/duration via `->beepFrequency(660)`, `->beepDuration(120)`, `->vibrateDuration(200)`. Server-side, `->distinctItems()` rejects duplicate codes on submit to match `->allowDuplicates(false)` in the browser.

<!-- file: docs/generating.md -->

# Generating QR Codes

> Back to [README](../README.md) · [Scanning](scanning.md) · [Batch collecting](collecting.md) · [Reference](reference.md)

Render QR codes in forms, tables, and infolists, offer downloads and bulk ZIP exports, or generate standalone via the facade.

## QR Generator components

![Interactive QR customizer](images/qr-customizer.png)

*Live preview of colours, size, margin and error correction.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Pages/QrCustomizer.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Pages/QrCustomizer.php).

### In Form Schemas

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrCodeDisplay;

QrCodeDisplay::make('qr')
    ->data(fn ($record) => $record?->uuid)
    ->size(200)
    ->color('#1e293b')
    ->caption('Scan to verify')
    ->downloadable();
```

### In Table Columns

![Products table with a QR column](images/products-table-qr-column.png)

*A QR column in a Filament table.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Resources/Products/Tables/ProductsTable.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Resources/Products/Tables/ProductsTable.php).

![QR preview modal opened from the table](images/products-qr-preview-modal.png)

*Clicking a QR opens the preview modal with download.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Resources/Products/Tables/ProductsTable.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Resources/Products/Tables/ProductsTable.php).

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Tables\Columns\QrColumn;

QrColumn::make('sku')
    ->thumbnailSize(48)
    ->modalSize(300)
    ->previewable()
    ->downloadable();
```

A previewable column owns its click: the thumbnail opens the preview instead of following the table's `recordUrl()`, which still applies to the other cells. With `->previewable(false)` the thumbnail links to the record like any other column.

Thumbnails and modal previews share a capped in-process render cache (clear it with `QrColumn::flushDataUriCache()`, for example between tests or in long-running workers) plus a persistent Laravel-cache L2 (`generator.cache_ttl`, default 86400s: an int is seconds, `null` keeps entries forever, `false` turns the L2 off while the in-process cache keeps working; `QrCodeService::persistentCache(false)` / `::cacheStore('redis')` to tune). The modal image loads lazily through a signed `filamentQrCode.image` route, so a 25-row table encodes 25 thumbnails instead of 50 mixed-size images — `->lazyModal(false)` restores eager data-URIs. The signed URL carries the full render spec (colors, error correction, logo, caption), so lazy previews match the inline renders exactly.

#### Image route security

The signed `filamentQrCode.image` route is safe by default (signatures stop tampering), and 1.0.1 adds opt-in hardening for apps where QR data or logo paths come from users. Invalid query input (missing `data`, out-of-range `size`, unknown `format` or `ec`, unparseable colours) always gets a 422, never a redirect or a 500; colours may be `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or bare hex. Every hardening key is off by default, so upgrading changes nothing until you set one:

```php
// config/qr-code.php
'generator' => [
    // ...
    'logo_base_paths' => [storage_path('app/qr-logos')],
],
'image_route' => [
    'ttl' => 60,             // preview URLs expire after an hour
    'throttle' => '60,1',    // 60 images per minute per client, then 429
    'strict_colors' => true, // #rrggbb only, else 422
],
```

- `logo_base_paths` resolves each logo with `realpath()` (so `../` and symlinks that escape are caught) and accepts only PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP files inside a listed directory. Inline renders (columns, entries, downloads, `QrCodeService`) skip a rejected logo and log a warning; the image route answers 422.
- `ttl` signs preview URLs with an `expires` parameter (expired links get 403) and caps the browser cache at the TTL.
- `qr-code:doctor` reports whether logos are restricted and flags base paths that do not exist.

### In Infolists

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Infolists\Components\QrEntry;

QrEntry::make('verification_code')
    ->size(200)
    ->caption('Official Verification QR');
```

### As a Download Action

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\QrFormat;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Tables\Actions\DownloadQrAction;

$table->actions([
    DownloadQrAction::make()
        ->qrData(fn ($record) => $record->verification_url)
        ->qrFileName(fn ($record) => "qr-{$record->id}")
        ->qrFormat(QrFormat::Png)
        ->qrImageSize(400)
        ->qrMargin(2),
]);
```

Both download actions share one render spec and default to black on white. Opt into the full surface to match a styled display — `->qrColor()`, `->qrBackgroundColor()`, `->qrErrorCorrection()`, `->qrLogo($path)`, `->qrCaption()` — and bulk filenames follow forced-PNG output (a logo or caption rasterizes) in their extension.

### As a Bulk ZIP Export

![Bulk ZIP export of selected products](images/products-bulk-zip-export.png)

*Select rows, then export their QR codes as one ZIP.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Resources/Products/Tables/ProductsTable.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Resources/Products/Tables/ProductsTable.php).

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\QrFormat;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Tables\Actions\DownloadQrBulkAction;

$table->bulkActions([
    DownloadQrBulkAction::make()
        ->qrData('sku') // attribute name, or fn ($record) => ...
        ->qrFileName(fn ($record) => $record->sku)
        ->qrFormat(QrFormat::Png)
        ->zipName('shelf-labels.zip'),
]);
```

Rows without data are skipped; the archive downloads as one ZIP (needs the PHP `zip` extension). For printed shelf labels, wrap any QR images in `.filament-qr-label-sheet` / `.filament-qr-label` — the print stylesheet hides camera UI and tiles three labels per row.

To test the export or reuse the renders elsewhere, `recordsToFiles(Collection $records): array` returns the same files without zipping: file name with extension => raw image bytes.

### Programmatic Standalone Generation

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Facades\FilamentQrCode;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\QrFormat;

// Generate data URI
$dataUri = FilamentQrCode::make()
    ->format(QrFormat::Svg)
    ->size(300)
    ->margin(2)
    ->color('#0f172a')
    ->backgroundColor('#ffffff')
    ->errorCorrection('M') // L, M, Q, H
    ->generate('https://example.com')
    ->toDataUri();

// Generate PNG with Text Overlay & Download
return FilamentQrCode::make()
    ->withText('BATCH #1024', 16, '#000000')
    ->generate('BATCH-1024')
    ->download('batch-1024'); // StreamedResponse download; stream() inlines
```

Rules that bite:

- `withText()` and `logo()` need raster output, so the service always returns PNG when either is set — regardless of whether `format()` was called before or after. Request PNG explicitly when overlaying.
- Invalid hex colors throw `InvalidArgumentException` instead of silently rendering black.
- `logo($path, $size)` forces error-correction level H for scannability.
- Identical payloads share the render cache, so tables with repeated values encode once.
- Other builder methods: `font($path)` sets the TTF used by `withText()`, `fileName($name)` sets the default download name (no extension), and `getRaw()` returns the encoded bytes.
- Static cache helpers on `QrCodeService`: `persistentCache(bool)`, `cacheStore(?string)`, `cacheTtl(int|false|null $seconds)` (overrides `generator.cache_ttl`; `null` clears the override) and `effectiveCacheTtl()` (the value in effect), `flushRenderCache()` (in-process) and `flushPersistentCache()` (Laravel cache).

### Common payloads without hand-escaping

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\QrPayload;

QrPayload::wifi('Shop Floor', 'secret-1');                    // WPA (nopass + hidden supported)
QrPayload::vcard(['firstName' => 'Siti', 'phone' => '...']);   // escaped vCard 3.0
QrPayload::mailto('ops@example.com', 'Stock alert', '...');   // mailto with subject/body
QrPayload::sms('+621234567', 'Arrived');                     // SMSTO
QrPayload::geo(-6.2, 106.8, 'Warehouse 7');                   // geo with query
```

<!-- file: docs/customizing.md -->

# Extending and customizing scan fields

Everything here is opt-in. A field that uses none of it behaves and renders exactly as before.

Worked examples: [POS checkout](recipes/pos.md) · [Goods receiving](recipes/warehouse.md) · [Work-order station](recipes/manufacturing.md) · [Label generator page](recipes/generator-page.md) · [Custom inputs](recipes/custom-input.md) · [Styling](recipes/styling.md).

## Find records yourself: `lookupUsing()`

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('sku')
    ->lookupUsing(fn (string $code) => Http::get("https://erp.test/items/{$code}")->json() ?: null);
```

The resolver replaces `lookup()` on that field. Return the record as a model, an array or an object. Return `null` or `false` to reject the scan with the usual "no record" message. The record then reaches `onScanned()`, `validateUsing()` and your stages. `ScanResult::$record` is typed `mixed`, and `recordKey()` reads `getKey()`, `id` or `key`.

To run the resolver only when the model lookup finds nothing, pass `fallback: true`:

```php
->lookup(Product::class, 'sku')
->lookupUsing(fn (string $code) => LegacyProduct::firstWhere('code', $code), fallback: true)
```

`lookup()` also takes closures for its model and column, for example `->lookup(fn (Get $get) => $get('type') === 'box' ? Box::class : Product::class)`.

Sequence steps work the same way. The resolver gets `$code`, `$values` (the other steps' values) and `$step`:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanStep;

ScanStep::make('serial')->lookupUsing(fn (string $code, array $values) => Serial::forPo($values['po'])->firstWhere('number', $code))
```

## Clean codes: `normalizeWith()` and `normalizeUsing()`

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('sku')
    ->normalizeWith(uppercase: true, stripPrefix: [']C1', 'SKU:'])   // trim is on by default
    ->normalizeUsing(fn (string $code) => str_replace(' ', '-', $code));
```

- `normalizeWith(trim: true, uppercase: false, stripPrefix: ...)` presets run in the browser too, so duplicate detection and step matching see the cleaned code. They run trim first, then strip the first matching prefix, then uppercase.
- `normalizeUsing()` runs on the server after the presets, before rules, lookup, closures and stages.
- On sequences, `normalizeWith()` applies to every step. Then `normalizeStepUsing()` runs, then the step's own `ScanStep::normalizeUsing(fn (string $code, array $values) => ...)`.

## Custom check stages: `pipe()`

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Contracts\ScanCheckStage;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanCheckContext;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanStep;

final class RejectOutOfStock implements ScanCheckStage
{
    public function __construct(private Inventory $inventory) {}   // resolved from the container

    public function check(ScanCheckContext $context): bool|string|null
    {
        return $this->inventory->has($context->record) ?: 'No stock left.';
    }
}

QrScanner::make('sku')->lookup(Product::class, 'sku')->pipe(RejectOutOfStock::class);
ScanStep::make('sku')->pipe(new RejectOutOfStock(app(Inventory::class)));
```

Stages run after the built-in rules, the lookup and the `validateUsing()` closures, in the order you add them. The first failing stage stops the scan. `true`/`null` passes, `false` rejects with the default message, and a string rejects with that message. A stage that throws rejects the scan as "could not be checked" and is reported. `ScanCheckContext` carries `code`, `source`, `record`, `component`, and for sequences also `step` and `values`. Stages also re-run when the form is submitted.

There is no config list of global stages. Use Filament's `configureUsing()` instead:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

// AppServiceProvider::boot()
QrScanner::configureUsing(fn (QrScanner $scanner) => $scanner->pipe(RejectOutOfStock::class));
```

## Normalize live scans

`scanFormat()` / `onScan()` / `onStepScanned()` never run on live camera or hardware scans — they are programmatic-only. Normalize live values instead:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('sku')
    ->normalizeUsing(fn ($rawValue) => strtoupper(trim((string) $rawValue)));

QrScanSequence::make([...])
    ->normalizeStepUsing(fn ($rawValue) => strtoupper(trim((string) $rawValue)));
```

Filament's `afterStateUpdated()` works too. Reject bad live scans with `->rejectWhen(fn ($state) => ..., 'message')`, which clears the value and dispatches `qr-scan-rejected`.

## Drive scans programmatically

Pair the programmatic-only hooks with their triggers in custom flows and tests:

```php
$scanner->formatScannedValue($raw); // runs scanFormat()
$scanner->triggerOnScan($value);    // runs onScan()
$sequence->formatScannedValue($raw);
$sequence->triggerOnStep($fieldKey, $value); // runs onStepScanned()
```

Every `handleScan()` / `triggerOnScan()` call also fires a `QrCodeScanned` event.

## Audit scans

Live scans stay client-side until they reach the server. Flip `audit.enabled` on to log server-observed scans through your log stack (`audit.channel`, default stack), or listen yourself:

```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Event;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Events\QrCodeScanned;

Event::listen(QrCodeScanned::class, function (QrCodeScanned $event): void {
    logger()->info("Scanned {$event->code} via {$event->source}");
});
```

The event carries `code`, `source`, `field`, and `context`.

## Step closures get `$get`, `$values` and `$step`

`label()`, `optional()`, `sticky()`, `allowDuplicates()` and lookup model/column closures on a `ScanStep` are evaluated by the sequence. That gives them Filament's usual injections (`$get`, `$set`, `$livewire`, `$record`) plus `$step` and, if they ask for it, `$values`:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanStep;

ScanStep::make('lot')->optional(fn (array $values) => ! Product::find($values['sku'] ?? null)?->tracksLots)
ScanStep::make('box')->label(fn (Get $get) => $get('mode') === 'inbound' ? 'Inbound box' : 'Box')
```

While `$values` are being read, a closure that asks for them again gets `[]`, so labels that read values can't recurse.

## Step hooks: `onStepAccepted()` / `onStepRejected()`

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanResult;

QrScanSequence::make([...])
    ->onStepAccepted(fn (string $step, ScanResult $result, array $values) => Log::info("{$step}: {$result->code}"))
    ->onStepRejected(fn (string $step, ScanResult $result) => Notification::make()->danger()->title($result->message)->send());
```

Hooks are for side effects only. Their return value is ignored, and they can't change whether a scan passes or its message. An exception thrown in a hook is reported and doesn't affect the scan. They get `$step`, `$result`, `$code`, `$record`, `$source` and `$values`.

## Richer events

`ScanAccepted` and `ScanRejected` carry `statePath`, `livewireClass` and `livewireId`. Sequence step events also carry `sequence` (the sequence state path) and `values`. Their `statePath` is the step's own path, for example `data.receipt.sku`. `ScanSequenceCompleted` carries `livewireClass` and `livewireId`. The `QrCodeScanned` context gains `state_path`. All new fields are optional constructor arguments, so existing listeners keep working.

## Macros

`QrScanner`, `QrScanSequence`, `QrCollector` and `ScanStep` are macroable:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanStep;

QrScanner::macro('sku', fn () => $this->lookup(Product::class, 'sku')->normalizeWith(uppercase: true));
ScanStep::macro('serial', fn () => $this->repeat()->allowDuplicates(false));
```

## Reusable field classes: `make:qr-scan-field`

```bash
php artisan make:qr-scan-field SkuScanner              # extends QrScanner
php artisan make:qr-scan-field ReceivingSequence --sequence
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=filament-qr-code-stubs  # customise the stubs
```

This creates `app/Filament/Forms/Components/{Name}.php` with a `setUp()` stub. It refuses to overwrite an existing file unless you pass `--force`. Published stubs in `stubs/filament-qr-code/` take precedence over the package's.

## Print sheets

Wrap QR images in `.filament-qr-label-sheet` / `.filament-qr-label` for a three-per-row shelf-label print sheet (the camera UI hides itself in print). Generator look (`size()`, `margin()`, `color()`, `backgroundColor()`, `errorCorrection()`, `caption()`, `withText()`, `logo()`) is in [generating.md](generating.md#qr-generator-components); `withText()` / `logo()` force PNG output.

## Styling

- **Extra attributes**: `->extraAttributes(['class' => 'my-scanner', 'data-test' => 'sku'])` merges onto the root of the scanner, sequence and collector.
- **Classes**: every part has a stable class, for example `fi-qr-scanner`, `fi-qr-scanner-input`, `fi-qr-scanner-modal`, `fi-qr-sequence-step`, `fi-qr-sequence-step-chip` and `fi-qr-collector-items`, plus a `data-qr-part` attribute such as `sequence.step-chip`.
- **CSS variables** (each defaults to the old value):

  | Variable | Default |
  |---|---|
  | `--fi-qr-viewfinder-bg` | `#000` |
  | `--fi-qr-viewfinder-radius` | `0.75rem` |
  | `--fi-qr-reticle-color` | `#22c55e` |
  | `--fi-qr-reticle-size` | `220px` (resized at runtime to the decoder crop) |
  | `--fi-qr-laser-color` | `#22c55e` |
  | `--fi-qr-flash-success` | `rgb(34 197 94)` |
  | `--fi-qr-flash-danger` | `rgb(239 68 68)` |

## Render hooks

```php
use Filament\Support\Facades\FilamentView;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\View\QrCodeRenderHook;

FilamentView::registerRenderHook(QrCodeRenderHook::SEQUENCE_STEPS_AFTER, fn () => view('receiving.legend'), scopes: 'data.receipt');
```

Available hooks: `SCANNER_START`, `SCANNER_END`, `SCANNER_MODAL_START`, `SCANNER_MODAL_END`, `SEQUENCE_START`, `SEQUENCE_END`, `SEQUENCE_STEPS_BEFORE`, `SEQUENCE_STEPS_AFTER`, `SEQUENCE_STEP_HEADER`, `COLLECTOR_START` and `COLLECTOR_END`. Scopes are the Livewire component class and the field state path. `SEQUENCE_STEP_HEADER` renders once into the Alpine step template, so it repeats on every step. Keep it static, or use Alpine expressions such as `x-text="f.label"`.

## Overriding parts of a view

The views are split into one file per part. Publish them with `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=filament-qr-code-views`, then keep only the files you change under `resources/views/vendor/filament-qr-code/components/`:

- `scanner/`: `input`, `camera-button`, `status`, `modal`, `modal-camera`, `modal-actions`
- `sequence/`: `header`, `camera-select`, `status`, `camera`, `steps`, `step`, `step-chip`, `step-value`
- `collector/`: `header`, `camera`, `items`

Parts share the parent view's variables (`$scanPayload`, `$statePath`, ...) and the Alpine scope. Keep `x-` bindings and `data-qr-*` attributes the JavaScript relies on.

<!-- file: docs/extending.md -->

# Extension points

Every seam the package offers, in one place. Each row links to the page that shows it in use.

## PHP

| Seam | Signature | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Record lookup | `->lookup(Model::class, 'column')`, `->lookupUsing(fn (string $code, ...) => mixed, fallback: false)` on `QrScanner` and `ScanStep` | [customizing.md](customizing.md#find-records-yourself-lookupusing) |
| Code normalization | `->normalizeWith(trim: true, uppercase: false, stripPrefix: null)`, `->normalizeUsing(fn ($rawValue) => string)`, `QrScanSequence::normalizeStepUsing()` | [customizing.md](customizing.md#clean-codes-normalizewith-and-normalizeusing) |
| Check stages | `->pipe(ScanCheckStage\|class-string ...$stages)`; `ScanCheckStage::check(ScanCheckContext $context): bool\|string\|null` | [customizing.md](customizing.md#custom-check-stages-pipe) |
| Reject rules | `QrScanner::rejectWhen(fn ($state) => bool, string\|Closure $message)` | [reference.md](customizing.md#normalize-live-scans) |
| Whole-set check | `QrScanSequence::validateAllUsing(array\|Closure $rules)`, `->onInvalidSequence(InvalidSequenceBehavior)` | [recipes/manufacturing.md](recipes/manufacturing.md#the-whole-bom) |
| Step closures | `$get`, `$values`, `$step` injected into every step closure | [customizing.md](customizing.md#step-closures-get-get-values-and-step) |
| Step hooks | `->onStepAccepted(fn ($step, $result, $code, $record, $source, $values) => ...)`, `->onStepRejected(...)`, `->onCompleted(fn (array $values) => ...)` | [customizing.md](customizing.md#step-hooks-onstepaccepted--onsteprejected) |
| Conditional steps | `ScanStep::when(fn ($values) => bool)` | [scanning.md](scanning.md#step-order-optional-skips-and-when) |
| Server control | `goToStep()`, `resetSequence()`, `refreshSequence()`, `setRepeatCount()` | [scanning.md](scanning.md#driving-a-sequence-from-page-code) |
| Laravel events | `QrCodeScanned`, `ScanAccepted`, `ScanRejected`, `ScanSequenceCompleted` | [events.md](events.md#laravel-events) |
| Macros | `QrScanner::macro()`, `QrScanSequence::macro()`, `QrCollector::macro()`, `ScanStep::macro()` | [customizing.md](customizing.md#macros) |
| Global defaults | Filament's `QrScanner::configureUsing(fn (QrScanner $field) => ...)` (any component), plus `config/qr-code.php` | [reference.md](reference.md#configuration) |
| Reusable fields | `php artisan make:qr-scan-field Name [--sequence]`, publishable stubs | [customizing.md](customizing.md#reusable-field-classes-makeqr-scan-field) |
| Payload builders | `QrPayload::wifi()`, `vcard()`, `mailto()`, `sms()`, `geo()` | [generating.md](generating.md#common-payloads-without-hand-escaping) |

## Markup and styling

| Seam | Signature | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Attributes | `->extraAttributes([...])` on every scan surface | [customizing.md](customizing.md#styling) |
| Classes | `fi-qr-*` class and `data-qr-part` marker on every part | [recipes/styling.md](recipes/styling.md#classes-and-css-variables) |
| CSS variables | `--fi-qr-viewfinder-bg`, `--fi-qr-viewfinder-radius`, `--fi-qr-reticle-color`, `--fi-qr-reticle-size`, `--fi-qr-laser-color`, `--fi-qr-flash-success`, `--fi-qr-flash-danger` | [recipes/styling.md](recipes/styling.md#classes-and-css-variables) |
