## Browser

| Seam | Signature | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per-element API | `el.qrScanner` on a `[data-qr-scanner]` root, `el.qrScanSequence` on a `[data-qr-sequence]` root: `feed()`, `pause()`, `resume()`, `setOptions()`, `getState()`, … | [scanning.md](scanning.md#per-element-api) |
| Window events | `qr-scanner-*`, `qr-sequence-*` control events; every `qr-*` event the package fires | [events.md](events.md) |
| Camera decoder | `FilamentQrCode.qrCameraCore.setDecoder(({ formats }) => module)`, `setDecoder(null)` | [scanning.md](scanning.md#camera-decoder-torch-and-zoom), [recipes/zxing-decoder.md](recipes/zxing-decoder.md) |
| Wedge router | `FilamentQrCode.router.register({ id, element, kind, scope, detection, accept, deliver, hold, ownsFocus })` returns `unregister()` | [scanning.md](scanning.md#your-own-inputs-in-the-hardware-router), [recipes/custom-input.md](recipes/custom-input.md) |
| Burst detection | `FilamentQrCode.createHardwareScannerHandler({ burstThresholdMs, minFastKeys, terminators, ... })`, `sanitizeScannedValue()` | [reference.md](reference.md#hardware_scanner) |
| Feedback | `FilamentQrCode.qrFeedback` (beep, vibrate, flash) | [scanning.md](scanning.md#feedback) |

## Related

- **Runtime control**: Change options at runtime, feed codes, pause, resume and reset scanners and sequences from page code, drive a sequence from PHP (`goToStep()`, `resetSequence()`, `setRepeatCount()`), make steps conditional with `ScanStep::when()`, and register your own inputs with `window.FilamentQrCode.router`. See [Runtime control](scanning.md#runtime-control).
- **Common payload builders**: `QrPayload::wifi()`, `::vcard()`, `::mailto()`, `::sms()`, `::geo()` build correctly escaped payloads — see [Common payloads](generating.md#common-payloads-without-hand-escaping).
- **Validate on submit**: `QrScanner::scanRules([...])` adds submit-time rules for the field; `QrCollector::distinctItems()` rejects duplicates server-side to match `->allowDuplicates(false)` in the browser.

<!-- file: docs/events.md -->

# Events

Every event the package fires or listens for. Browser events are dispatched on `window` unless noted. Listen with Alpine (`x-on:qr-scanned.window="..."`), `window.addEventListener(...)`, or Livewire's `#[On('qr-scanned')]` (Livewire forwards browser events dispatched on `window`).

## Browser events the package fires

### Scanner (`QrScanner`)

| Event | `detail` | Fired when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `qr-scanned` | `{ value, field, nextField, source, recordKey?, mode }` | any accepted scan; `recordKey` is set when a server check found a record |
| `qr-scan-accepted` | `{ value, field, source, recordKey, mode }` | a server-checked scan passed |
| `qr-scan-rejected` | `{ value, field, source, message, mode }` | a server-checked scan failed; also dispatched from PHP with `{ message }` when a `rejectWhen()` predicate matches |
| `qr-scan-duplicate` | `{ value, field, source, mode }` | the same code again within the field's cooldown |
| `qr-scan-dropped` | `{ value, field, source }` | a busy continuous field already held one queued scan |
| `qr-scan-paused` | `{ field }` | a continuous field with `pauseOnReject()` paused after a rejection, or the field was paused |
| `qr-scan-resumed` | `{ field }` | the operator or page code resumed a paused field |
| `qr-hardware-scanned` | `{ value, field }` | a keyboard-wedge burst was delivered to a field |

`source` is `camera`, `hardware`, `upload` or `manual`. `mode` is `single` or `continuous` (see [Continuous mode](scanning.md#continuous-mode)).

### Sequence (`QrScanSequence`)

| Event | `detail` | Fired when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `qr-sequence-step` | `{ field, value, index, source, skipped? }` | a step accepted a code; `skipped` lists optional steps the code jumped over |
| `qr-sequence-completed` | `{ results, submitted? }` | the last step landed and the whole-set check passed; `submitted` is the `autoSubmit()` outcome |
| `qr-sequence-edited` | `{ field, value }` | the operator typed or corrected a step value |
| `qr-sequence-rejected` | `{ field, value, message, source }` | a step check rejected a code |
| `qr-sequence-invalid` | `{ field, message, values }` | `validateAllUsing()` failed, on completion or on an early finish of a `repeat(n)` step |
| `qr-scan-dropped` | `{ value, field, source }` | a burst arrived while the sequence was busy and one was already queued |

### Collector (`QrCollector`, `QrCollectAction`)

| Event | `detail` | Fired when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `qr-collector-item-added` | `{ code }` | each accepted batch scan |

### Hardware router (`QrHardwareScannerListener` and every wedge target)

| Event | `detail` | Fired when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `qr-scan-routed` | `{ value, target, kind, reason, burstId }` | the router delivered a burst; `reason` is `modal`, `focus`, `first-listening`, `fallback` or `queued` |
| `qr-scan-unrouted` | `{ value }` | no target took the burst (see `fallback_to_any_input`) |
| `qr-hardware-scanned` | `{ value, field }` | the listener wrote a burst into a form input |
| `qr-scan-deliver` | `{ value }` | dispatched on the target input itself (bubbles, cancelable); a scanner field cancels it to take the code. Internal, but you can listen on your own inputs |

## Browser events you send

Send these on `window`, or with `$this->dispatch(...)` from PHP. `field` picks the target: a scanner matches its state path (`data.sku`), field name (`sku`) or component key (`form.sku`); a sequence matches its key or state path. Leave `field` out to reach every component of that kind. Details and examples: [Runtime control](scanning.md#window-events).

| Event | `detail` |
| --- | --- |
| `qr-scanner-feed` | `{ field, code, source? }` |
| `qr-scanner-pause` / `qr-scanner-resume` / `qr-scanner-reset` / `qr-scanner-refresh` | `{ field }` |
| `qr-scanner-set-options` | `{ field, options }` |
| `qr-sequence-feed` | `{ field, code, source? }` |
| `qr-sequence-go-to` | `{ field, step }` |
| `qr-sequence-reset` | `{ field, values? }` |
| `qr-sequence-pause` / `qr-sequence-resume` / `qr-sequence-refresh` | `{ field }` |
| `qr-sequence-set-options` | `{ field, options }` |
| `qr-sequence-set-repeat` | `{ field, step, count }` (display only; use `setRepeatCount()` in PHP to change the server check too) |
| `qr-sequence-editable` | `{ enabled }`: switch every sequence between editable and read-only step inputs |

The PHP helpers `goToStep()`, `resetSequence()` and `refreshSequence()` dispatch `qr-sequence-go-to`, `qr-sequence-reset` and `qr-sequence-refresh` for you.

## Laravel events

All live in `Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Events`. Listen with `Event::listen()` or a listener class.

| Event | Properties | Fired when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `QrCodeScanned` | `string $code`, `string $source`, `?string $field`, `array $context` | every scan the server sees: `handleScan()`, `triggerOnScan()`, an accepted server check, an accepted sequence step, a `QrCollectAction` scan |
| `ScanAccepted` | `ScanResult $result`, `string $field`, `?string $statePath`, `?string $livewireClass`, `?string $livewireId`, `?string $sequence`, `array $values` | a server check passed (a field, or a sequence step: then `$field` is the step key, `$sequence` the sequence's state path and `$values` the values at the time) |
| `ScanRejected` | same as `ScanAccepted` | a server check failed |
| `ScanSequenceCompleted` | `array $values`, `?string $statePath`, `?string $livewireClass`, `?string $livewireId` | a sequence completed on the server and the whole-set check passed |

With `audit.enabled`, the package's own `Listeners\LogQrCodeScanListener` logs every `QrCodeScanned` (see [Audit scans](customizing.md#audit-scans)).

# Reference

> Back to [README](../README.md) · [Scanning](scanning.md) · [Batch collecting](collecting.md) · [Generating](generating.md) · [Customizing](customizing.md)

Recipes: [POS checkout](recipes/pos.md) · [Goods receiving](recipes/warehouse.md) · [Work-order station](recipes/manufacturing.md) · [Label generator page](recipes/generator-page.md) · [Custom inputs](recipes/custom-input.md) · [Styling](recipes/styling.md). Upgrading from an earlier release: [UPGRADE.md](../UPGRADE.md).

Configuration, browser events and translations. How-to material lives in [customizing.md](customizing.md) and [extending.md](extending.md); every public method is in the [API map](api.md).

## Public API and `@internal`

Everything documented here and in the guides is public API and follows semver. Classes and methods tagged `@internal` in a docblock (render cache and spec classes, client payloads, the Livewire and Filament hooks a component must keep public) are not: they can change in any release, including a minor or patch release. Don't call or extend them from app code.

## Configuration

Publish the config to tune defaults (`config/qr-code.php`):

```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag="filament-qr-code-config"
```

Per-component options override these defaults:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\BarcodeFormat;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('sku')
    ->fps(25)
    ->qrbox(250) // responsive max; the decode box scales to the viewfinder
    ->formats([BarcodeFormat::QrCode, BarcodeFormat::Code128])
    ->preferRearCamera()
    ->cameraControls() // torch / zoom when the camera supports them; false hides them
    ->hardwareScanner(terminators: ['Enter', 'Tab'], minBarcodeLength: 2)
    ->minFastKeys(3) // consecutive fast keystrokes before a terminator counts
    ->beepFrequency(880)
    ->beepDuration(80)
    ->vibrateDuration(100)
    // server-checked fields only (see scanning.md → Feedback)
    ->beep(success: true, error: true)
    ->vibrate(success: [100], error: [80, 60, 80])
    ->flash();
```

### `hardware_scanner`

| Key                   | Default            | Meaning                                            |
| --------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`             | `true`             | master switch (components also gate individually)  |
| `burst_threshold_ms`  | `50`               | max gap between keystrokes counted as one burst    |
| `min_barcode_length`  | `2`                | shorter bursts are treated as typing               |
| `min_fast_keys`       | `3`                | consecutive fast gaps required before a terminator counts; `3` rejects fast typists, `1` restores the 0.x behaviour |
| `fallback_to_any_input` | `true`           | page-global listener may fill the first empty form input when no focused or registered field is free; `false` dispatches `qr-scan-unrouted` instead |
| `scan_timeout_ms`     | `150`              | flush window for terminator-less guns (0 disables) |
| `prevent_form_submit` | `true`             | swallow the terminator key during bursts           |
| `default_terminators` | `['Enter', 'Tab']` | gun suffix keys ending a scan                      |
| `default_scope`       | `'focus'`          | where a `QrScanner` catches wedge scans: `'focus'` (only while focused) or `'page'` (also when no scan field has focus); override with `->hardwareInput(scope:)` |

Auto-repeat keystrokes (a held-down key) never count toward a burst.

#### Hardware routing

Every wedge consumer (`QrScanner`, `QrHardwareScannerListener`, `QrCollector`, `QrScanSequence`) registers with one page-wide input router, so each burst is handled exactly once. The router picks the owner in this order:

1. the `QrScanner` whose camera modal is open;
2. the focused scan field (a focused `QrScanner`, or a focused field registered with a listener);
3. the first listening target on the page, in page order: page-scope `QrScanner` fields (`->hardwareInput(scope: HardwareInputScope::Page)`), collectors, sequences and each empty field registered with a listener (ranked by the field's own position);
4. the listener's `fallback_to_any_input`;
5. otherwise `qr-scan-unrouted`.

A field that can't take the burst (busy checking a scan, too short for its `min_barcode_length`) is skipped and the next target gets it. When the burst lands somewhere other than the focused input, the characters the gun typed into that input are removed again, unless the input (or an ancestor) has the `data-qr-ignore` attribute.

These values are the defaults behind every scan surface (`QrScanner`, `QrScanSequence`, `QrCollector`, `QrHardwareScannerListener`, `QrCollectAction`): each component ships them to the browser as one payload (`getScanPayload()`), and any explicit setter (`->fps()`, `->sound()`, `->hardwareScanner()`, …) wins over config.

The Station Listener adds its own routing switch:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrHardwareScannerListener;

QrHardwareScannerListener::make(['sku'])
    ->fallbackToAnyInput(false); // no first-empty-input fallback; dispatch qr-scan-unrouted instead
```

### `feedback`

| Key                   | Default  |
| --------------------- | -------- |
| `sound`               | `true`   |
| `beep_frequency`      | `880` Hz |
| `beep_duration_ms`    | `80`     |
| `vibrate`             | `true`   |
| `vibrate_duration_ms` | `100`    |
| `success`             | `['sound' => true, 'vibrate' => [100], 'flash' => true]` |
| `error`               | `['sound' => true, 'vibrate' => [80, 60, 80], 'flash' => true]` |

### `camera`

| Key                  | Default | Meaning                                                                                  |
| -------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fps`                | `25`    | decode attempts per second; auto-degrades to 12 when unrestricted and not explicitly set |
| `qrbox`              | `250`   | _maximum_ decode-box edge; the real box scales to the viewfinder (wide band for 1D)      |
| `prefer_rear_camera` | `true`  | rear heuristic; the remembered `localStorage` choice wins                                |
| `controls`           | `true`  | torch / zoom controls, shown only when the running camera reports the capability         |

### `scan`

| Key                            | Default   | Meaning |
| ------------------------------ | --------- | ------- |
| `cooldown_ms`                  | `1500`    | repeat window for fields with server checks (`cooldown()`) |
| `clear_on_reject`              | `true`    | clear the field on a rejected live scan (`clearOnReject()`) |
| `continuous.display`           | `'empty'` | continuous fields after an accepted scan: `'empty'` or `'last_code'` (`continuousDisplay()`) |
| `continuous.pause_on_reject`   | `false`   | `false` shows the error and keeps scanning; `true` pauses until dismissed (`pauseOnReject()`) |
| `continuous.keep_camera_open`  | `false`   | `false` closes the camera after each scan (`keepCameraOpen()`) |
| `continuous.cooldown_ms`       | `300`     | repeat window for continuous fields (`cooldown()` wins) |
| `sync_options`                 | `'morph'` | when the browser picks up server option changes: `'morph'` (every re-render) or `'refresh'` (only on a `qr-scanner-refresh` / `qr-sequence-refresh` event); `syncOptions()` per field |

### `sequence`

Every key of `qr-code.sequence`; each has a per-component setter that wins over config. Sequence events are in [events.md](events.md#sequence-qrscansequence).

| Key                  | Default          | Meaning |
| -------------------- | ---------------- | ------- |
| `on_invalid`         | `'jump_to_step'` | a failed `validateAllUsing()`: `'jump_to_step'` or `'restart'` (`onInvalidSequence()`) |
| `auto_submit`        | `false`          | call `submit_method` once the sequence completes (`autoSubmit()`) |
| `submit_method`      | `'submit'`       | the Livewire method `autoSubmit()` calls |
| `reset_after_submit` | `false`          | clear non-sticky steps after a successful submit (`resetAfterSubmit()`) |
| `continuous`         | `false`          | start over after every completed sequence (`continuous()`) |
| `repeat_complete`    | `'advance'`      | a full `repeat(n)` step: `'advance'` or `'wait'` (`onRepeatComplete()`) |
| `finish_code`        | `null`           | the scan that finishes a waiting or open-ended repeat step (`finishWith()`) |

### `generator`

`size` (300), `margin` (2), `format` (`svg`), `foreground_color`, `background_color`, `error_correction` (`M`), `cache_ttl` (86400; `null` = forever, `false` = L2 off), `cache_store` (`null` = default store), `logo_base_paths` (`null` = any readable path; a list of directories logos must live in — see [Image route security](generating.md#image-route-security)).

### `image_route`

| Key             | Default | Meaning |
| --------------- | ------- | ------- |
| `ttl`           | `null`  | minutes a lazy-preview URL stays valid (`temporarySignedRoute`); also caps `Cache-Control` `max-age` at the TTL (never above a day). `null` = never expires |
| `throttle`      | `null`  | rate limit for the image route, e.g. `'60,1'` (60 per minute per client); excess requests get 429 |
| `strict_colors` | `false` | require `#rrggbb` colours on the image route (default accepts `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or bare hex); anything else gets 422 |

### `audit`

| Key       | Default | Meaning |
| --------- | ------- | ------- |
| `enabled` | `false` | log every server-observed scan (`QrCodeScanned`) — see [Audit scans](customizing.md#audit-scans) |
| `channel` | `null`  | log channel for the audit lines; `null` uses the default stack |

## Translations

All UI strings live under the `filament-qr-code::ui` translation namespace (`resources/lang/en/ui.php`, plus Indonesian in `resources/lang/id/ui.php`). Publish with:

```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag="filament-qr-code-translations"
```

and translate per locale.

Camera errors and screen-reader announcements are translated too: the browser components receive them from PHP, so a published `ui.php` covers them. The announcement keys take placeholders: `announce_added` (`:code`, `:count`), `announce_step_added` (`:code`, `:step`), `announce_field_added` (`:code`, `:field`) and `announce_rejected` (`:reason`); `camera_device` takes `:id`.

### Screen-reader announcements

The `QrScanner` field, the collector, the collect-action modal and the scan sequence each have a visually hidden polite live region (`data-qr-part="announcer"`, `role="status"`). It reads each accepted scan ("Added SKU-1 to SKU" for the field, using its label; "Added ABC-1 (3 items)"; "Added PO-1 to PO") and each rejection ("Rejected: Unknown PO", or "Rejected: This code was rejected." when there is no message) once; the same message is not repeated within 3 seconds. Camera errors stay in a `role="alert"` region.

Rapid scans do not pile up. Each message replaces the region's text rather than adding to it. The first message is written straight away; messages that arrive within 500 ms of it are coalesced, so only the newest one is written when the window ends. A burst of scans therefore reads the first and the latest result, not every one in between.

Announcements are on by default. `QrScanner`, `QrCollector` and `QrScanSequence` can turn them off or change the wording:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrCollector;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('badge')
    ->announcements(false); // or a Closure returning bool

QrCollector::make('items')
    ->announceUsing(fn (string $code, bool $accepted, ?string $reason, ?string $field): ?string => $accepted
        ? "Checked in {$code}"
        : null); // null keeps the default text
```

The `announceUsing()` closure receives `$code`, `$accepted`, `$reason` (the rejection message, or null) and `$field` (the field label, or the step label in a scan sequence). HTML tags in the returned text are stripped. The closure runs on the server, so setting it adds one Livewire request per scan; when several scans are in flight, only the newest reply is announced.

<!-- file: docs/faq.md -->

# FAQ

> Back to [README](../README.md) · [Getting started](getting-started.md) · [Scanning](scanning.md) · [Reference](reference.md)

Each answer below describes what the package code does. For symptoms and fixes, see the [Troubleshooting table](../README.md#troubleshooting).

## Why is there no torch (flashlight) button on my iPhone?

The torch and zoom controls only appear when the running camera track reports that capability (`getCapabilities()` returns `torch` or `zoom`). The package never guesses. If the browser doesn't report torch support, which is common on iOS Safari, the button stays hidden and the rest of the scanner works as usual. `->cameraControls(false)` (or `camera.controls => false`) hides the controls everywhere.

## Why does the camera say it needs a secure context?

Browsers only allow camera access on secure origins: `https`, or `localhost` during development. When `window.isSecureContext` is false, the scanner shows the `camera_needs_secure_context` message instead of asking for permission, and it never loads the decoder. Serve the panel over `https`. For testing on a phone over the LAN, use an `https` tunnel or a trusted local certificate. The image-upload fallback, typing and Hardware Scanners still work over plain `http`.

## Does scanning work offline?

The browser side has no external dependency. The scanner bundle and the camera decoder are compiled into `resources/dist` and served from your app by `php artisan filament:assets`, with no CDN. When the browser has a native `BarcodeDetector` that covers every requested format, it is used, and otherwise the bundled `html5-qrcode` decoder loads. The decoder still has to be downloaded from your server once. Scanned values go into the Livewire state, and anything server-side needs a connection: lookups, `validateUsing()`, `onScanned()`, events and form submit. The package has no offline queue.

## Do I need special drivers for a handheld gun?

No, as long as the gun is in keyboard (HID / keyboard-wedge) mode. The Hardware Scanner Interceptor tells a gun from a person by timing:

- the keystrokes arrive within `burst_threshold_ms` (50 ms) of each other;
- there are at least `min_fast_keys` (3) fast gaps in a row;
- the code is at least `min_barcode_length` (2) characters long;
- a terminator key (`Enter` or `Tab`) ends the scan, or, for guns without one, `scan_timeout_ms` passes.

The terminator is swallowed so the form doesn't submit. Slow Bluetooth guns can lower `->minFastKeys(1)`. Guns in serial (SPP / COM port) mode don't type keystrokes, so the package doesn't see them. See [`hardware_scanner`](reference.md#hardware_scanner).

## A gun scan lands in the wrong field. Who gets the burst?

One page-wide router hands every burst to exactly one owner. The order is: the open camera modal, then the focused scan field, then the first listening target on the page, then the Station Listener's first-empty-input fallback, and finally a `qr-scan-unrouted` event. See [Hardware routing](reference.md#hardware-routing). To keep a search box out of the fallback, use `->fallbackToAnyInput(false)`. To keep the router's hands off an input entirely, add `data-qr-ignore`.

## Does it work with several panels?

Yes. The service provider registers the JS and CSS once for every panel, so `->plugin(FilamentQrCodePlugin::make())` is optional on each one. Register it on a panel only if you call `FilamentQrCodePlugin::get()` there. Each panel theme needs its own `@source` line for the package views ([Getting started, step 3](getting-started.md#3-add-the-package-views-to-your-theme)). Config is app-wide. To vary a default per panel, use component setters or `configureUsing()`.

<!-- file: docs/ai.md -->

# AI guide

> For coding agents (and the people reviewing their work) adding `mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code` to a Laravel + Filament v5 app. Back to [README](../README.md) · [API map](api.md) · [Getting started](getting-started.md)

This guide is written for agents that build *with* the package. Agents working *on* the package should read `AGENTS.md` in the repository instead. The whole doc set is also available as one file in [`llms-full.txt`](../llms-full.txt), with an index in [`llms.txt`](../llms.txt). The words below (QR Scanner Field, Station Listener, Scan Sequence Container, Batch Collector Scanning, Hardware Scanner, Scan Feedback, …) follow the project vocabulary in [CONTEXT.md](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code/blob/main/CONTEXT.md).

## Component picker

| The user wants… | Use | Namespace |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one input filled by camera, image upload, typing or a gun | QR Scanner Field: `QrScanner` | `Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components` |
| a gun driving several fields, no camera UI (POS, station) | Station Listener: `QrHardwareScannerListener` | `Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components` |
| one camera filling many fields in a fixed order | Scan Sequence Container: `QrScanSequence` + `ScanStep` | `…\Forms\Components`, `…\Support` |
| focus to jump from one scan field to the next | Sequential Field Scanning: `QrScanner::nextField()` | `Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components` |
| many scans appended to one list (stocktake, receiving) | Batch Collector Scanning: `QrCollector` (form) or `QrCollectAction` (table/repeater action) | `…\Forms\Components`, `…\Tables\Actions` |
| show a QR in a form / table / infolist | `QrCodeDisplay` / `QrColumn` / `QrEntry` | `…\Forms\Components`, `…\Tables\Columns`, `…\Infolists\Components` |
| download one QR / many as a ZIP | `DownloadQrAction` / `DownloadQrBulkAction` | `Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Tables\Actions` |
| generate an SVG/PNG in PHP | `FilamentQrCode` facade or `QrCodeService` | `…\Facades`, `…\Services` |
| a Wi-Fi, vCard, mailto, SMS or geo payload | `QrPayload` | `Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support` |

## Do

- **Write out every import**, including enums (`BarcodeFormat`, `ScanMode`, …) and Filament classes (`Filament\Schemas\Schema`). Nothing is global.
- **Set `->formats([...])`** whenever you know the symbology. It speeds up decoding and cuts false positives.
- **Check on the server** with `lookup()`, `lookupUsing()`, `validateUsing()`, `rejectWhen()` or `pipe()`. Live scans write straight into the Livewire state, and the server checks are what reject bad codes.
- **Normalize live scans** with `normalizeWith()` / `normalizeUsing()` (or `normalizeStepUsing()` on a sequence).
- **Give a `QrScanSequence` a `->statePath()`** (or `->key()`), and read it on submit with `mergeSequenceState()` / `isSequenceComplete()`.
- **Name fields exactly** in `nextField()` and `QrHardwareScannerListener::make([...])`. Dot paths like `items.0.sku` work, and `sku` never matches `parent_sku`.
- **Add the `@source` line** for the package views to the panel theme, and run `php artisan filament:assets` after installing or updating.
- **Use component setters** for per-field options. They always win over `config/qr-code.php`.

## Don't

- **Don't rely on `scanFormat()`, `onScan()` or `onStepScanned()` for live scans.** They are programmatic-only and run only through `formatScannedValue()`, `triggerOnScan()` and `triggerOnStep()`. Use `normalizeUsing()`, `onScanned()` / `onRejected()` or `afterStateUpdated()` instead.
- **Don't add your own `keydown` listener for guns.** Register custom inputs with `window.FilamentQrCode.router.register()` so each burst has exactly one owner.
- **Don't call or extend anything tagged `@internal`** (see below).
- **Don't hand-merge sequence state** with `array_merge($this->data, …)`. Use `mergeSequenceState()`.
- **Don't promise a torch button.** It only appears when the camera reports the capability, and iOS Safari usually doesn't.
- **Don't test camera scanning over plain `http`.** It needs `https` or `localhost`.
- **Don't edit `resources/dist`** in the vendor directory. It is a compiled bundle.

## Common mistakes

| Symptom | Mistake | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Class "QrScanner" not found` | missing `use` statement | `use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;` |
| unstyled Start/Stop buttons | the theme doesn't scan the package views | add `@source '../../../../vendor/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code/resources/views/**/*';` and rebuild |
| normalizer never runs | put on `scanFormat()` | move it to `normalizeUsing()` |
| bad codes get saved | only `scanRules()` (which run on submit) | add `lookup()` / `validateUsing()` for live rejection |
| a sequence submit misses values | reading `$this->data` directly | `$sequence->mergeSequenceState($this->form->getState())` |
| a gun scan fills a search box | the Station Listener fell back to the first empty input | `->fallbackToAnyInput(false)` and listen for `qr-scan-unrouted` |
| a slow Bluetooth gun is ignored | `min_fast_keys` is 3 | `->minFastKeys(1)` |
| a table page is slow with many QRs | turned off `lazyModal()` or the cache | keep `->lazyModal()` (the default) and `generator.cache_ttl` |

## Public API and `@internal`

Everything in the [API map](api.md) follows semver. Members tagged `@internal` are not public API and can change in any release, including patches: render specs and caches, client payloads (`toClient()`), check pipelines, and the Livewire/Filament hooks that have to stay `public`. The API map leaves them out on purpose. If a task seems to need one, look for the public setter or the extension seam in [extending.md](extending.md) instead.

## Examples with full imports

A QR Scanner Field with a server-side lookup:

```php
use App\Models\Product;
use Filament\Schemas\Schema;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\BarcodeFormat;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

public static function configure(Schema $schema): Schema
{
    return $schema->components([
        QrScanner::make('sku')
            ->formats([BarcodeFormat::Code128, BarcodeFormat::Ean13])
            ->normalizeWith(uppercase: true)
            ->lookup(Product::class, 'sku')
            ->onScanned(fn (string $code, $record) => logger()->info("Scanned {$code}")),
    ]);
}
```

A Station Listener routing gun scans into two fields:

```php
use Filament\Forms\Components\TextInput;
use Filament\Schemas\Schema;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrHardwareScannerListener;

public static function configure(Schema $schema): Schema
{
    return $schema->components([
        QrHardwareScannerListener::make(['sku', 'quantity'])->autoFocusNext(),
        TextInput::make('sku'),
        TextInput::make('quantity'),
    ]);
}
```

A Scan Sequence Container with checked steps:

```php
use App\Models\Product;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanStep;

QrScanSequence::make()
    ->statePath('receipt')
    ->steps([
        ScanStep::make('po')->label('Purchase order')->validateUsing(['regex:/^PO-\d+$/']),
        ScanStep::make('sku')->lookup(Product::class, 'sku'),
    ])
    ->autoSubmit();
```

Batch Collector Scanning into a list:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\BarcodeFormat;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrCollector;

QrCollector::make('scanned_items')
    ->formats([BarcodeFormat::QrCode])
    ->allowDuplicates(false)
    ->distinctItems();
```

Showing and downloading a QR:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Tables\Actions\DownloadQrAction;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Tables\Columns\QrColumn;

QrColumn::make('sku')->thumbnailSize(48)->previewable();

DownloadQrAction::make()->qrData(fn ($record) => $record->sku);
```

Generating in PHP:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Facades\FilamentQrCode;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\QrPayload;

$dataUri = FilamentQrCode::make()
    ->size(300)
    ->generate(QrPayload::wifi('Shop Floor', 'secret-1'))
    ->toDataUri();
```

## Where to look next

- Every public method: [api.md](api.md). Every config key: [reference.md](reference.md#configuration).
- Browser and Laravel events: [events.md](events.md). Extension seams: [extending.md](extending.md).
- Worked flows: [recipes](recipes/pos.md) (POS, goods receiving, work-order station, label page, custom inputs, styling, ZXing decoder).

<!-- file: docs/recipes/custom-input.md -->

# Recipe: custom inputs and reusable fields

Three ways to bring your own input into the scanner: feed codes from another device, share the keyboard-wedge router with your own widget, or package a configured scanner as a field class.

## Feed codes from anywhere

An RFID reader, a WebSocket, or a test can push a code into a scanner or a sequence. It goes through exactly the same checks as a scan:

```blade
<div x-data x-on:rfid-read.window="$dispatch('qr-sequence-feed', { field: 'data.station', code: $event.detail.tag, source: 'hardware' })"></div>
```

From PHP (for example after a broadcast event):

```php
$this->dispatch('qr-scanner-feed', field: 'data.scan', code: $tag, source: 'hardware');
```

Or from JavaScript with the element API:

```js
await document.querySelector('[data-qr-sequence]').qrScanSequence.feed('OP-001', 'hardware');
```

`source` is `camera`, `hardware`, `upload` or `manual`; it reaches `ScanResult::$source`, the hooks and the events. Typed (`manual`) codes never skip an optional step.

## Run the checks yourself

A field class (or a Livewire action that holds the field) can run the same normalization and checks a scan gets, without going through the browser:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\ScanInput;

$code = $field->normalizeScannedCode($rawTag);           // normalizeWith() presets, then normalizeUsing()
$result = $field->runScanChecks($code, ScanInput::Hardware); // rules, lookup, closures, piped stages

if (! $result->passes) {
    // $result->message explains why; $result->record holds the looked-up record otherwise
}
```

`runScanChecks()` expects an already normalized code and stops at the first failing check. Both methods are on `QrScanner` (through `InteractsWithScans`); they don't fire the scan hooks or events.

## Share the keyboard-wedge router

Every wedge burst on the page has one owner. Register your own input so it takes part instead of fighting the scanners for keystrokes:

```js
const unregister = window.FilamentQrCode.router.register({
    id: 'rfid-keypad',
    element: document.querySelector('#rfid'),
    kind: 'custom',
    scope: 'focus',                          // or 'page': also when nothing else is focused
    detection: { minBarcodeLength: 4 },
    accept: (code) => /^\d{10}$/.test(code), // return false to pass the burst on
    deliver: (code) => window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('rfid-read', { detail: { tag: code } })),
});
```

Call `unregister()` when the widget goes away (Alpine's `destroy()`, or `livewire:navigating`).

## A reusable field class

```bash
php artisan make:qr-scan-field SkuScanner            # extends QrScanner
php artisan make:qr-scan-field StationSequence --sequence
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=filament-qr-code-stubs  # optional: edit the stubs first
```

```php
<?php

namespace App\Filament\Forms\Components;

use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\ScanMode;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

class SkuScanner extends QrScanner
{
    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        parent::setUp();

        $this->lookup(Product::class, 'sku')
            ->normalizeWith(uppercase: true)
            ->mode(ScanMode::Continuous);
    }
}
```

Use it like any field: `SkuScanner::make('scan')->onScanned(...)`. For a setting that should apply to every scanner in the app instead, use `QrScanner::configureUsing()` in a service provider.


---

<!-- file: docs/recipes/generator-page.md -->

# Recipe: a label generator page

A Filament page that prints QR labels for your own records (products, work orders, badges) and downloads single codes as SVG or PNG, built only on the generator API. Use it when the built-in `QrCodeColumn` / `QrCodeEntry` don't fit, for example a printable sheet.

Runs in the example app: `/admin/qr-labels` (`app/Filament/Pages/QrLabels.php`).

## Building the codes

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\QrFormat;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Facades\FilamentQrCode;

/** @return list<array{code: string, caption: string}> */
public function labels(): array
{
    return array_values(match ($this->data['set'] ?? 'products') {
        'products' => Product::query()->orderBy('sku')->get()->map(fn (Product $product): array => ['code' => $product->sku, 'caption' => $product->name])->all(),
        'badges' => array_map(fn (array $badge): array => ['code' => $badge['badge'], 'caption' => $badge['name']], app(BadgeDirectory::class)->active()),
        default => [],
    });
}

public function previewDataUri(string $code): string
{
    return FilamentQrCode::make()
        ->format(QrFormat::Svg)               // SVG: crisp on screen and paper, no image extension needed
        ->size((int) ($this->data['size'] ?? 160))
        ->margin(1)
        ->color($this->validColor())
        ->generate($code)
        ->toDataUri();
}

public function download(string $code): ?StreamedResponse
{
    // Only codes on the current sheet: the method is callable from the browser.
    if (! in_array($code, array_column($this->labels(), 'code'), true)) {
        return null;
    }

    return FilamentQrCode::make()
        ->format(($this->data['format'] ?? 'svg') === 'png' ? QrFormat::Png : QrFormat::Svg)
        ->size(400)
        ->margin(2)
        ->color($this->validColor())
        ->errorCorrection('M')
        ->generate($code)
        ->download('qr-'.$code);              // the extension follows the format
}

protected function validColor(): string
{
    $color = (string) ($this->data['color'] ?? '#000000');

    return preg_match('/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/', $color) === 1 ? $color : '#000000';
}
```

## The sheet

![Printable QR label sheet](../images/qr-labels-print-sheet.png)

*The print-only label sheet.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Pages/QrLabels.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Pages/QrLabels.php).

```blade
<div class="filament-qr-label-sheet">
    @foreach ($this->labels() as $label)
        <figure class="filament-qr-label">
            <img src="{{ $this->previewDataUri($label['code']) }}" alt="{{ $label['code'] }}">
            <figcaption>{{ $label['code'] }} · {{ $label['caption'] }}</figcaption>
            <x-filament::link class="filament-qr-no-print" wire:click="download(@js($label['code']))">Download</x-filament::link>
        </figure>
    @endforeach
</div>
<x-filament::button class="filament-qr-no-print" x-on:click="window.print()">Print</x-filament::button>
```

The package's print stylesheet lays out `.filament-qr-label-sheet` / `.filament-qr-label` as a grid and hides `.filament-qr-no-print` when printing.

## Notes

- PNG needs the `imagick` or `gd` extension (imagick is preferred when both are loaded); `php artisan qr-code:doctor` tells you which one is in use. SVG has no requirements.
- Validate user-chosen colours and sizes before passing them on, as above.
- Generated codes aren't stored; for many labels, cache `previewDataUri()` per code and style.
- To print what a scanner reads, keep the label value identical to what your `lookup()` column holds (or what `normalizeWith()` produces).

<!-- file: docs/recipes/manufacturing.md -->

# Recipe: work-order station

An assembly station: the operator scans their badge, a work order, a rework reason when the order is a rework, then one label per component until the unit is built. It uses every P2 extension point: a non-Eloquent lookup, a conditional step, a custom check stage, a whole-set check, step hooks and runtime control.

Runs in the example app: `/admin/manufacturing` (`app/Filament/Pages/ManufacturingStation.php`).

## The sequence

![Work order sequence with all steps captured](../images/work-order-sequence.png)

*A sequential work order with every step scanned.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Pages/WorkOrderSequence.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Pages/WorkOrderSequence.php).

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanResult;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanStep;

QrScanSequence::make()
    ->statePath('station')
    ->steps([
        ScanStep::make('operator')
            ->label('Operator badge')
            ->validateUsing(['regex:/^OP-\d{3}$/'])
            ->lookupUsing(fn (string $code): ?array => app(BadgeDirectory::class)->find($code)) // not Eloquent
            ->sticky(),
        ScanStep::make('order')
            ->label('Work order')
            ->lookup(AssemblyOrder::class, 'number', fn ($query) => $query->where('status', 'open'))
            ->sticky(),
        ScanStep::make('rework_reason')
            ->label('Rework reason')
            ->when(fn (array $values): bool => (bool) AssemblyOrder::findOpen($values['order'] ?? null)?->is_rework)
            ->validateUsing(['regex:/^RW-\d{2}$/']),
        ScanStep::make('components')
            ->label('Components')
            ->validateUsing(['regex:/^CMP-\d{3}:\d{4}$/'])   // component SKU, then serial
            ->repeat()
            ->finishWith('DONE')
            ->pipe(ComponentBelongsToBom::class),
    ])
    ->normalizeWith(uppercase: true)
    ->validateAllUsing(fn (array $values): array => ['components' => $this->missingComponents($values)])
    ->onStepAccepted(fn (string $step, ScanResult $result) => $this->logActivity($step, $result))
    ->onStepRejected(fn (string $step, ScanResult $result) => $this->logActivity($step, $result))
    ->autoSubmit()
    ->resetAfterSubmit()
    ->editable(false),
```

## A lookup that isn't Eloquent

`lookupUsing()` replaces the model lookup. Return anything (here an array) or `null` to reject with the "no record" message. The value reaches `ScanResult::$record`, your hooks and your stages:

```php
final class BadgeDirectory
{
    /** @return array{badge: string, name: string, active: bool}|null */
    public function find(string $badge): ?array
    {
        $operator = Http::get("https://hr.example.test/badges/{$badge}")->json();

        return ($operator['active'] ?? false) ? $operator : null;
    }

    /** @return list<array{badge: string, name: string, active: bool}> */
    public function active(): array
    {
        return Http::get('https://hr.example.test/badges', ['active' => 1])->json();
    }
}
```

The work order model keeps the BOM lookups the stage and the page share:

```php
final class AssemblyOrder extends Model
{
    public function bomLines(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(BomLine::class);
    }

    public static function findOpen(?string $number): ?self
    {
        return $number === null ? null : self::query()->where('number', $number)->where('status', 'open')->first();
    }

    /** @return array<string, int> component SKU => quantity per unit */
    public function bom(): array
    {
        return $this->bomLines()->pluck('quantity', 'sku')->map(fn ($quantity): int => (int) $quantity)->all();
    }
}
```

## A check stage

Stages run after the step's rules, its lookup and its `validateUsing()` closures, and again on submit. Return `true`/`null` to pass, `false` for the default message, or a string message:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Contracts\ScanCheckStage;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanCheckContext;

final class ComponentBelongsToBom implements ScanCheckStage
{
    public function check(ScanCheckContext $context): bool|string|null
    {
        $order = AssemblyOrder::findOpen($context->values['order'] ?? null);

        if ($order === null) {
            return 'Scan a work order first.';
        }

        $sku = explode(':', $context->code, 2)[0];
        $needed = $order->bom()[$sku] ?? 0;

        if ($needed === 0) {
            return "{$sku} is not on the BOM for {$order->number}.";
        }

        // Live scans see the codes collected so far; submit re-runs see the
        // full list, this code included. Count the others either way.
        $fitted = count(array_filter(
            (array) ($context->values['components'] ?? []),
            fn (mixed $code): bool => $code !== $context->code && explode(':', (string) $code, 2)[0] === $sku,
        ));

        return $fitted < $needed ? true : "All {$needed} × {$sku} are already fitted.";
    }
}
```

Stages are resolved from the container, so constructor injection works. To add one to every sequence step or scanner in the app, use `configureUsing()` in a service provider (there is no config list):

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::configureUsing(fn (QrScanner $scanner) => $scanner->pipe(RejectBlockedCodes::class));
```

## The whole BOM

`components` is open-ended: the operator scans `DONE` (or presses the step's **Done** button) when the unit is assembled. Finishing runs `validateAllUsing()`:

```php
public function missingComponents(array $values): ?string
{
    $order = AssemblyOrder::findOpen($values['order'] ?? null);
    $fitted = array_count_values(array_map(fn ($code) => explode(':', (string) $code, 2)[0], $values['components'] ?? []));

    $missing = [];

    foreach ($order?->bom() ?? [] as $sku => $quantity) {
        if (($short = $quantity - ($fitted[$sku] ?? 0)) > 0) {
            $missing[] = "{$short} × {$sku}";
        }
    }

    return $missing === [] ? null : 'BOM incomplete: missing '.implode(', ', $missing).'.';
}
```

`validateAllUsing()` also runs when a counted step (`repeat(3)`) is finished early with `finishWith()`: the operator sees what the BOM is missing ("BOM incomplete: missing …") instead of the generic repeat count message, and `qr-sequence-invalid` fires.

## Hooks and runtime control

![Manufacturing station with paused banner](../images/manufacturing-paused.png)

*A station paused at runtime shows the paused banner.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Pages/ManufacturingStation.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Pages/ManufacturingStation.php).

`onStepAccepted()` / `onStepRejected()` receive `$step`, `$result`, `$code`, `$record`, `$source` and `$values`, and can't change the outcome:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanResult;

public function logActivity(string $step, ScanResult $result): void
{
    $text = match (true) {
        ! $result->passes => "{$result->code}: {$result->message}",
        $step === 'operator' && is_array($result->record) => "{$result->record['name']} signed in",
        default => "{$step}: {$result->code}",
    };

    array_unshift($this->activity, ['step' => $step, 'text' => $text, 'rejected' => ! $result->passes]);
}

public function restartUnit(): void { $this->sequence()->resetSequence(); }                    // keeps badge and order
public function changeOperator(): void { $this->sequence()->resetSequence(keepSticky: false); }
public function backToComponents(): void { $this->sequence()->goToStep('components'); }
```

```blade
<x-filament::button wire:click="restartUnit">Restart unit</x-filament::button>
<x-filament::button x-on:click="$dispatch('qr-sequence-pause', { field: 'data.station' })">Pause scanning</x-filament::button>
<x-filament::button x-on:click="$dispatch('qr-sequence-resume', { field: 'data.station' })">Resume</x-filament::button>
```

## How it behaves

- `op-001` is cleaned to `OP-001` in the browser and on the server (`normalizeWith()`), then found in the directory.
- Badge and work order are sticky: after a build the next unit starts at the first empty step.
- On a rework order the rework step becomes active; on other orders it is skipped, greyed out and not required.
- A component that isn't on the BOM, one too many, or a duplicate serial is rejected with its message; scanning continues.
- `DONE` with parts missing jumps back to components with "BOM incomplete: …". A complete unit auto-submits.


---

<!-- file: docs/recipes/pos.md -->

# Recipe: POS checkout with continuous scanning

A cashier page where a handheld scanner (keyboard wedge) or the camera adds products to a cart, one line per SKU, without touching the mouse.

Runs in the example app: `/admin/pos-checkout` (`app/Filament/Pages/PosCheckout.php`).

## The form

```php
use Filament\Forms\Components\Repeater;
use Filament\Forms\Components\TextInput;
use Filament\Schemas\Components\Utilities\Get;
use Filament\Schemas\Components\Utilities\Set;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\ContinuousDisplay;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\HardwareInputScope;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Enums\ScanMode;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanner;

QrScanner::make('scan')
    ->label('Scan item')
    ->mode(ScanMode::Continuous)
    ->hardwareInput(scope: HardwareInputScope::Page)
    ->normalizeWith(uppercase: true)            // a handheld set to lower case still matches
    ->lookup(Product::class, 'sku')
    ->onScanned(function (Product $record, Get $get, Set $set): void {
        $set('lines', CartLines::add($get('lines') ?? [], $record));
    })
    // Page switches: options follow the server on every re-render.
    ->continuousDisplay(fn (): ContinuousDisplay => $this->keepLastCode ? ContinuousDisplay::LastCode : ContinuousDisplay::Empty)
    ->pauseOnReject(fn (): bool => $this->pauseOnReject)
    ->keepCameraOpen(fn (): bool => $this->keepCameraOpen)
    ->dehydrated(false),

Repeater::make('lines')
    ->schema([
        TextInput::make('sku')->disabled(),
        TextInput::make('name')->disabled(),
        TextInput::make('quantity')->numeric()->minValue(1),
    ])
    ->addable(false),
```

Toggle `keepLastCode`, `pauseOnReject` or `keepCameraOpen` with `wire:model.live` checkboxes and the scanner picks up the new options in place: the camera, a queued scan and the field state all survive. Don't wrap the form in a changing `wire:key`; that re-creates the scanner and was only needed before 0.6.

## Merging lines

The package calls `onScanned()` once per accepted code; merging is the app's job:

```php
final class CartLines
{
    /** @param array<int|string, array{sku: string, name: string, quantity: int}> $lines */
    public static function add(array $lines, Product $product): array
    {
        foreach ($lines as $key => $line) {
            if ($line['sku'] === $product->sku) {
                $lines[$key]['quantity']++;

                return $lines;
            }
        }

        $lines[] = ['sku' => $product->sku, 'name' => $product->name, 'quantity' => 1];

        return $lines;
    }
}
```

## Pause and resume buttons

Window events reach the scanner by its state path, field name or component key:

```blade
<x-filament::button color="gray" x-on:click="$dispatch('qr-scanner-pause', { field: 'data.scan' })">Pause scanning</x-filament::button>
<x-filament::button color="gray" x-on:click="$dispatch('qr-scanner-resume', { field: 'data.scan' })">Resume</x-filament::button>
```

From PHP, `$this->dispatch('qr-scanner-pause', field: 'data.scan')` does the same.

## How it behaves

![POS checkout with scanned items](../images/pos-checkout.png)

*Scanned SKUs land as line items with live totals.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Pages/PosCheckout.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Pages/PosCheckout.php).

- **Page scope**: with nothing focused, a wedge scan goes to the first listening field on the page, here the scan field. A focused scan field always wins, so another scanner on the page still works when the cashier clicks into it.
- **Empty after each scan** (`continuousDisplay`, default `Empty`): the field is ready for the next item.
- **Unknown code**: the lookup rejects it, the error tone plays and the message shows under the field. Scanning continues (`pauseOnReject()` to stop until the cashier confirms).
- **Camera**: closes after each scan by default; `keepCameraOpen()` for scan-scan-scan with a phone.
- **Same item twice**: two lines merge into quantity 2. Scans of the same code closer than 300 ms are treated as a camera re-read and ignored (`qr-code.scan.continuous.cooldown_ms`). `normalizeWith()` runs first, so `prd-1001` and `PRD-1001` count as the same code.
- **Fast bursts**: one scan is queued while the previous one is checked; more fire `qr-scan-dropped`.

Defaults for all of this live in `config/qr-code.php` under `scan.continuous`.

# Recipe: styling a scanner or sequence

From least to most invasive: CSS classes and variables, render hooks, then a published sub-view. Prefer the first two; they survive package updates.

The example app's manufacturing station (`/admin/manufacturing`) uses all three.

## Classes and CSS variables

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;

QrScanSequence::make()
    ->statePath('station')
    ->extraAttributes(['class' => 'mfg-station']),
```

```css
/* resources/css/filament/admin/theme.css */
.mfg-station {
    --fi-qr-viewfinder-radius: 1.25rem;
    --fi-qr-reticle-color: #f59e0b;
    --fi-qr-laser-color: #f59e0b;
    --fi-qr-flash-success: rgb(16 185 129);
}

/* Each step row is .fi-qr-sequence-step with data-qr-step-active="true|false". */
.mfg-station .fi-qr-sequence-step[data-qr-step-active='false'] {
    text-decoration: line-through;
}
```

The full variable list is in [Customizing](../customizing.md). Parts carry `data-qr-part` attributes (`sequence.step`, …), which are also safe to target in tests.

## Render hooks

Add markup at fixed points without touching the views. Scope a hook to one field by its state path:

```php
use Filament\Support\Facades\FilamentView;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\View\QrCodeRenderHook;

FilamentView::registerRenderHook(
    QrCodeRenderHook::SEQUENCE_STEPS_AFTER,
    fn (): View => view('filament.hooks.mfg-legend'),
    scopes: 'data.station',
);
```

Hooks: `SCANNER_START`, `SCANNER_END`, `SCANNER_MODAL_START`, `SCANNER_MODAL_END`, `SEQUENCE_START`, `SEQUENCE_END`, `SEQUENCE_STEPS_BEFORE`, `SEQUENCE_STEPS_AFTER` `SEQUENCE_STEP_HEADER` (the same markup in every step header: steps render client-side, so it can't vary per step), and `COLLECTOR_START` / `COLLECTOR_END`.

## A published sub-view

When markup has to change, publish the views and keep only the file you edit:

```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=filament-qr-code-views
# keep resources/views/vendor/filament-qr-code/components/sequence/step-chip.blade.php, delete the rest
```

Keep the Alpine bindings the package relies on (`results`, `currentFieldIndex`, `idx`, `isSticky(...)`) and add to them, e.g. a pin on sticky steps:

```blade
<span data-mfg-sticky-pin x-show="isSticky(f.key)" x-cloak>📌</span>
```

A published view applies to every scanner and sequence in the app and stops following package changes: diff it against the package's copy after each upgrade (see [UPGRADE](../../UPGRADE.md)).

<!-- file: docs/recipes/warehouse.md -->

# Recipe: goods receiving with a handheld scanner

A receiving desk scans a purchase order once, then for every item a SKU, an optional lot and one serial per unit. A keyboard-wedge scanner drives it without focusing anything; the item is saved as soon as it's complete.

Runs in the example app: `/admin/goods-receiving` (`app/Filament/Pages/GoodsReceiving.php`).

## The sequence

![Goods receiving sequence completed](../images/goods-receiving-received.png)

*The receiving sequence after every step is captured.* See the full example app: [`app/Filament/Pages/GoodsReceiving.php`](https://github.com/mmuqiitf/filament-qr-code-example/blob/main/app/Filament/Pages/GoodsReceiving.php).

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanResult;
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Support\ScanStep;

QrScanSequence::make()
    ->statePath('receipt')
    ->steps([
        ScanStep::make('po')
            ->label('Purchase order')
            ->validateUsing(['regex:/^PO-\d+$/'])
            ->sticky(),                                   // kept for every item on the PO
        ScanStep::make('sku')
            ->label('SKU')
            ->lookup(Product::class, 'sku'),
        ScanStep::make('lot')
            ->label('Lot (if labelled)')
            ->validateUsing(['regex:/^LOT-[A-Z0-9]+$/'])
            ->optional(),                                 // a serial scanned here gives way to the serials step
        ScanStep::make('serials')
            ->label('Serial numbers')
            ->validateUsing(['regex:/^SN-[A-Z0-9-]+$/'])
            ->repeat(fn (): int => max(1, $this->quantity)), // follows a page field; the k / n counter updates live
    ])
    ->validateAllUsing(function (array $values): array {
        $prefix = 'SN-'.($values['sku'] ?? '').'-';

        foreach ($values['serials'] ?? [] as $serial) {
            if (! str_starts_with((string) $serial, $prefix)) {
                return ['serials' => "Serials must belong to {$values['sku']}."];
            }
        }

        return [];
    })
    ->onStepRejected(fn (string $step, ScanResult $result) => logger()->notice("Receiving: {$step} rejected {$result->code}", ['message' => $result->message]))
    ->autoSubmit(fn (): bool => $this->autoSubmit)
    ->resetAfterSubmit()
    ->editable(false),
```

## Saving the item

`autoSubmit()` calls the page's `submit()` once the item is complete. `getState()` re-runs every step check and `validateAllUsing()`, so a typed or tampered value can't slip through:

```php
use Mmuqiitf\FilamentQrCode\Forms\Components\QrScanSequence;

public function submit(): void
{
    $receipt = $this->form->getState()['receipt'] ?? [];
    $product = Product::query()->where('sku', $receipt['sku'])->firstOrFail();

    GoodsReceipt::create([
        'po_number' => $receipt['po'],
        'product_id' => $product->getKey(),
        'lot_number' => $receipt['lot'] ?? null,
        'serials' => array_values($receipt['serials']),
    ]);

    // Next item: keep the sticky PO. (resetAfterSubmit() does this for auto-submits;
    // a manual "Receive item" button needs it here.)
    $this->sequence()->resetSequence();
}

protected function sequence(): QrScanSequence
{
    $sequence = $this->form->getComponent(fn ($component): bool => $component instanceof QrScanSequence);

    if (! $sequence instanceof QrScanSequence) {
        throw new LogicException('The form has no QrScanSequence.');
    }

    return $sequence;
}
```

## How it behaves

- **Order** `po, sku, lot?, serials`: on an item without a lot label, the operator scans the first serial at the lot step. It fails the lot's rule but fits the serials step, so the lot is skipped (`skipped: ['lot']`) and the serial lands there. Typed corrections never skip.
- **Sticky PO**: stays across items. The step's **Clear** button (or scanning it again after selecting it) changes it.
- **Serials**: duplicates are rejected; each code has a remove button for mis-scans. The count follows `$this->quantity` on every re-render, with no re-mount.
- **Whole item**: `validateAllUsing()` runs when the last serial is in. On failure the sequence jumps back to the failing step (`onInvalidSequence()`, default `JumpToStep`).
- **Side effects**: `onStepRejected()` (and `onStepAccepted()`) are for logging and notifications only. Their return value is ignored and an exception inside is reported without changing the scan.
- **Events**: listen to `ScanRejected` / `ScanAccepted` instead when the audit lives elsewhere. Step events carry `statePath` (`data.receipt.serials`), `sequence` and `values`.

<!-- file: docs/recipes/zxing-decoder.md -->

# Recipe: use ZXing as the camera decoder

The camera decoder is swappable. By default the package uses the browser's native
`BarcodeDetector` when it supports every format the field asks for (Chrome on Android,
macOS and ChromeOS, Edge) and falls back to the bundled html5-qrcode otherwise. If you
would rather decode everything with [ZXing](https://github.com/zxing-js/browser), drop
in the adapter below. ZXing is not bundled; you install it in your own app.

```bash
npm install @zxing/browser @zxing/library
```

## The adapter

A decoder is a module with the html5-qrcode surface the scanner, sequence and collector
use. Save this as `resources/js/zxing-decoder.js`:

```js
import { BrowserCodeReader, BrowserMultiFormatReader } from '@zxing/browser';
import { BarcodeFormat, DecodeHintType } from '@zxing/library';

class ZxingScanner {
    constructor(elementId, { formatsToSupport = [] } = {}) {
        this.elementId = elementId;
        const hints = new Map();
        if (formatsToSupport.length > 0) {
            hints.set(DecodeHintType.POSSIBLE_FORMATS, formatsToSupport);
        }
        this.reader = new BrowserMultiFormatReader(hints);
        this.controls = null;
        this.video = null;
        this.paused = false;
    }

    static async getCameras() {
        const devices = await BrowserCodeReader.listVideoInputDevices();

        return devices.map((device) => ({ id: device.deviceId, label: device.label }));
    }

    async start(cameraId, config, onSuccess) {
        this.video = document.createElement('video');
        this.video.muted = true;
        this.video.playsInline = true;
        this.video.style.width = '100%';
        document.getElementById(this.elementId).appendChild(this.video);

        this.controls = await this.reader.decodeFromVideoDevice(cameraId, this.video, (result) => {
            if (result && !this.paused) {
                onSuccess(result.getText(), result);
            }
        });
    }

    async stop() {
        this.controls?.stop();
        this.controls = null;
        this.video?.remove();
        this.video = null;
    }

    pause() {
        this.paused = true;
    }

    resume() {
        this.paused = false;
    }

    async scanFile(file) {
        const url = URL.createObjectURL(file);
        try {
            return (await this.reader.decodeFromImageUrl(url)).getText();
        } finally {
            URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
        }
    }

    // Optional: lets the built-in torch / zoom buttons work.
    getRunningTrackCapabilities() {
        return this.video.srcObject.getVideoTracks()[0].getCapabilities();
    }

    applyVideoConstraints(constraints) {
        return this.video.srcObject.getVideoTracks()[0].applyConstraints(constraints);
    }
}

export default { Html5Qrcode: ZxingScanner, Html5QrcodeSupportedFormats: BarcodeFormat };
```

`Html5QrcodeSupportedFormats` maps the PHP `BarcodeFormat` names (`QR_CODE`, `CODE_128`,
`EAN_13`, …) to the decoder's own ids. ZXing's `BarcodeFormat` enum uses the same names, so
it can be passed straight through.

## Register it

Load it once, before anyone opens a camera. A Filament render hook in your panel provider
works well, or import it from your app bundle:

```js
import zxing from './zxing-decoder.js';

window.FilamentQrCode.qrCameraCore.setDecoder(() => zxing);
```

The loader receives `{ formats }` (the field's PHP format names), so you can mix decoders,
for example ZXing only for `MAXICODE` and the default everywhere else:

```js
const { qrCameraCore } = window.FilamentQrCode;

qrCameraCore.setDecoder(async ({ formats }) =>
    formats.includes('MAXICODE') ? (await import('./zxing-decoder.js')).default : qrCameraCore.defaultDecoderLoader({ formats }),
);
```

Call `setDecoder(null)` to go back to the default.
